issues.author: Syko80
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The compute/virtual-machine module uses the nested_networkInterface.bicep module.  The default is to pass in to that module the setting as below..

`enableAcceleratedNetworking: contains(nicConfiguration, 'enableAcceleratedNetworking') ? nicConfiguration.enableAcceleratedNetworking : true`

Source: https://github.com/Azure/ResourceModules/blob/main/modules/compute/virtual-machine/main.bicep

However the default setting for the param is set to false 
`param enableAcceleratedNetworking bool = false`

Source https://github.com/Azure/ResourceModules/blob/main/modules/compute/virtual-machine/modules/nested_networkInterface.bicep

Considering the default value is false, and therefore if a user doesnt specifically set the value, then it makes sense that the value passed to the nested module should also default to false.

I discovered this to be an issue because I was expecting the default behaviour to be false and the vmsize i was creating didn't support network acceleration and therefore caused a Conflict failure.


### To reproduce

Create a VM and do not specifically set the enableAcceleratedNetworking value

The NIC will be created as 'Accelerated Networking - true' where the user would expect this to be false (unless you read every line of code like me!) because 

param enableAcceleratedNetworking bool = false

### Code snippet

```Bicep
BUILD BICEP FILE
param virtualMachines array

module buildvms2 './modules/compute/virtual-machine/main.bicep' = [for vm in virtualMachines: {
  name: 'my-vm'
  params:{
    location: 'eastus'
    name: vm.vmName
    adminUsername: vm.adminUsername
    adminPassword: vm.adminPasswordOrKey
    imageReference: vm.imageReference
    nicConfigurations: [
      {
        enableAcceleratedNetworking: false
        deleteOption: 'Delete'
        ipConfigurations: [
          {
            name: 'ipconfig01'
            subnetResourceId: '${resourceGroup().id}/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/${vm.networkname}/subnets/${vm.subnetname}'
          }
        ]
        nicSuffix: '-nic-01'
      }
    ]
    osDisk: {
      diskSizeGB: 50
      managedDisk: {
        storageAccountType: 'Premium_LRS'
      }
    }
    osType: 'Linux'
    secureBootEnabled: true
    vmSize: vm.vmsize
  
  }
}

BICEP PARAM FILE

using './vm_from_azure_resources.bicep'

param virtualMachines = [
  {
    vmName: 'bicepvm'
    vmsize: 'Standard_B1s'   //this vm size needs acceleration turned off
    imageReference: {
      publisher: 'Canonical'
      offer: '0001-com-ubuntu-server-jammy'
      sku: '22_04-lts-gen2'
      version: 'latest'
    }
    adminUsername: 'myadminuser'
    adminPasswordOrKey: 'somegreatpassword123!!'
    networkname: '<existing vnet nam>'
    subnetname: '<existing subnet name>'
  }
```


### Relevant log output

```Shell
"statusMessage": {
        "error": {
          "additionalInfo": null,
          "code": "VMSizeIsNotPermittedToEnableAcceleratedNetworking",
          "details": [],
          "message": "Virtual machine /subscriptions/<my-subscription>/resourceGroups/<my-rg>/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/bicepvm has size Standard_B1s, which is not compatible with enabling accelerated networking on network interface(s) on the VM......."
```

issues.author: tyconsulting
issues.body:
### Description

# Benefit
Tags with `hidden-` prefix are not visible in the Azure portal except in the JSON view.  by adding the additional hidden tags for CARML module names and versions allows customers to:

- Collect internal usage and inventory data for the consumption of the module. When a module requires update, customers can easily find out which resources need to be updated using simple Azure Resource Graph (ARG) queries.
- Provides the ability to control the usage of `-prerelease` module versions being deployed outside of testing environments using Azure Policy

**I am happy to raise PR to implement this feature since @ahmadabdalla and I have already developed this feature in a customer's environment.**

# How to implement

I have implemented this feature in a customer's environment. here's what I did:

1. update the pipeline tasks to write the full `major.minor.patch` version number to the version.json in the run time, before the module publishing step.
2. update each CARML module to add the module name and version. version number is extracted from `version.json` file:

```bicep
var moduleVersion = loadJsonContent('./version.json').version

var mergedTags = union(tags, {
    'hidden-module_name': 'storage/storage-account'
    'hidden-module_version': moduleVersion
  })
```
3. Pass the `mergedTags` to the `tags` property of the resources

# How to consume the hidden module name and version tags

## Collecting internal usage telemetry data

Here are some sample ARG queries:

### Get all Overlay module usage

```kusto
resources
| where tags['hidden-module_name']  matches regex '.'
| summarize count() by type
```

### Get all Key Vaults deployed using Overlay module and show version

```kusto
resources
| where type =~ "microsoft.keyvault/vaults"
| where tags['hidden-module_name'] =~ 'key-vault/vault'
| project name, tags
| mvexpand tags
| extend tagKey = tostring(bag_keys(tags)[0])
| extend tagValue = tostring(tags[tagKey])
| distinct name, tagKey, tagValue
| where tagKey =~ "hidden-module_version"
| project KeyVaultName = name, OverlayModuleVersion = tagValue
```

## Restrict resources to be deployed using prerelease overlay module versions

Here's a sample policy definition I have created to restrict the use of `-prerelease' versions:

```json
{
  "name": "pol-restrict-prerelease-overlay-module-versions",
  "properties": {
    "displayName": "Restrict resources to be deployed using prerelease overlay module versions",
    "description": "Prerelease module versions are published for testing purposes only. They are not intended for production use and they have not gone through code review and validation. This policy restricts resources from being deployed using prerelease overlay module versions.",
    "metadata": {
      "category": "Code Vulnerability",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "preview": false,
      "depreciated": false
    },
    "mode": "Indexed",
    "parameters": {
      "effect": {
        "type": "String",
        "metadata": {
          "displayName": "Effect",
          "description": "Enable or disable the execution of the policy"
        },
        "allowedValues": [
          "Audit",
          "Deny",
          "Disabled"
        ],
        "defaultValue": "Deny"
      }
    },
    "policyRule": {
      "if": {
        "allOf": [
          {
            "field": "tags[hidden-module_version]",
            "exists": true
          },
          {
            "field": "tags[hidden-module_version]",
            "like": "*-prerelease"
          }
        ]
      },
      "then": {
        "effect": "[parameters('effect')]"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
There are a few things we could consider for AVM such as
- Instead of loading the version.json (with only major.minor) take the actual version during publishing like

```bicep
  tags: {
    'hidden-version': replace('-..--..-', '.', '-')
  }
```

- Have an input parameter (bool) that allows you to control if you want this or not
- etc.

issues.author: eriqua
issues.body:
### Description

The implementation of diagnostic settings applied to resources related to the main resource (nested or cross referenced) should be aligned and possibly simplified.

- List modules applying diagnostic on related resources and propose a consistent implementation for all
- Parameter names should be aligned (e.g., sometimes we have `pipDiagnostic` sometimes `publicIPDiagnostic`)
- Update guidelines in the wiki

Initial list:
- natgateways and virtual network gateways cross reference PIP and specify pip diagnostic settings parameters
- azure firewall and bastion host cross reference PIP and do not specify pip diagnostic settings parameters, they are implemented directly into the cross referenced module
- VM and VMSS apply diagnostic on pip and nics in a different way as they do not cross reference pip and nic modules. They specify diagnostic settings parameters for both pip and nic
   > Note: VMSS pip diagnostic implementation is probably not working (to be tested)

Note: Diagnostic on cross referenced should also import shared common types

issues.author: AlexanderSehr
issues.body:
### Description

If resources support tags:

- You MUST be able to set tags for the parent resource via the 'tags' input par/var
- You MUST also be able to set tags for child and cross-referenced resources
- By default, all tags set for the primary resource will automatically be passed down to the child and cross-referenced resources
- This can be overridden to specify alternate tags for child and cross-referenced resources
- This is not a merge/union with the parent resource tags, so therefore a consumer must duplicate tag keys/values if they wish them to exist on both

TODO: 
- Check for consistent implementation in modules. Should align with: https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/specs/shared/interfaces/#tags (especially **no** union of tags)
- Implement test to validate

issues.author: donheerschap
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [X] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/web/site

### (Optional) Module Version

_No response_

### Description

If you use identity to authenticate to the underlying storage account of the functionapp you require roleassignments to be done.

But when following the AVM patterns as is you will encounter a cycle of dependencies (The expression is involved in a cycle ("fn" -> "fnstg").bicep(BCP080))

As is would look something like this (which won't work)
```bicep
module fnstg 'br/public:avm/res/storage/storage-account:0.9.1' = { // Storage account for the function app backend (where the function app code is stored)
  name: '${deployment().name}-functionStorage'
  scope: resourceGroup(rgName)
  dependsOn: [
    rg
  ]
  params: {
    name: fnstgName
    location: location
    roleAssignments: [
      {
        principalId: fn.outputs.systemAssignedMIPrincipalId
        roleDefinitionIdOrName: 'Storage Blob Data Owner'
      }
      {
        principalId: fn.outputs.systemAssignedMIPrincipalId
        roleDefinitionIdOrName: 'Storage Blob Queue Data Contributor'
      }
      {
        principalId: fn.outputs.systemAssignedMIPrincipalId
        roleDefinitionIdOrName: 'Storage Account Contributor'
      }
    ]
  }
}

module fn 'br/public:avm/res/web/site:0.3.9' = { // Function app which will run the python code
  name: '${deployment().name}-function'
  scope: resourceGroup(rgName)
  dependsOn: [
    rg
    asp
    fnstg
  ]
  params: {
    name: fnName
    location: location   
    kind: 'functionapp,linux'
    serverFarmResourceId: asp.outputs.resourceId
    siteConfig: {
      pythonVersion: '3.11'
      linuxFxVersion: 'python|3.11'
    }
    appSettingsKeyValuePairs: {
      FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME: 'python'
      FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION: '~4'
      WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE: '1' // Required to be able to deploy from a package
    }
    managedIdentities: {
      systemAssigned: true // Creates a managed identity for the function app to access other azure resources
    }
    storageAccountResourceId: fnstg.outputs.resourceId
    storageAccountUseIdentityAuthentication: true // Required to be able to access the storage account without access keys
  }
}
```

You could work around by creating seperate role assignment resource depending on these two and call the fnstg as existing resource for the scope of the resource roleassignment, but I think this could be done better in the web/site module.

**Proposed solution**
When `storageAccountUseIdentityAuthentication: true` and `!empty(storageAccountResourceId)` these 3 roleassignments should be created in the module

issues.author: cecheta
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [X] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Description

There is an intermittent error that can occur when checking the deployment status during CI:

```
  VERBOSE: 12:13:38 - Checking deployment status in 8 seconds
  VERBOSE: Resource deployment Failed.. (1/3) Retrying in 5 Seconds.. 
  
  VERBOSE: An error occurred while sending the request.
  
  VERBOSE: Deploying with deployment name [a-p-ap-b-max-t2-20240729T1207070374Z]
  VERBOSE: Setting context to subscription [***]
  VERBOSE: Using Bicep v0.29.47
  ...
...
```

When this occurs, a new deployment is started, however the first deployment is actually still ongoing. The second deployment is then likely to fail because there are essentially two deployments going on at the same time.

Perhaps a retry could be added when checking the deployment status?

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Description

This issue is based on [this proposal](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Verified-Modules/issues/1296).

The idea:
- Update both the AVM specs & modules to add the `@export()` annotation to their types (if they should be 'importable') 
- This would allow anybody using the modules to also important any custom type and re-use it when defining their own interface that uses the module
- We already do this today in a few cases where parent modules reference exported types of their child modules. This approach would just go a bit further as you could also import the type directly from the Public Bicep Registry.
https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/blob/34c5bf10c4cb75fbd51db3fd4a030a7cb6d6bd7b/avm/res/compute/gallery/main.bicep#L251

This should be done for both the top-level modules, as well as the child-modules. The later won't be available for import just yet, but once we finally manage to find a scalable way to publish child-modules, they would automatically become available too.

Just one to add to the module notes:

Notes
Considerations
This template is using a Tenant level deployment, meaning the user/principal deploying it needs to have the [proper access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/deploy-to-tenant#required-access)

If owner access is excessive, the following rights roles will grant enough rights:

Automation Job Operator at tenant level (scope '/')
Management Group Contributor at the top management group that needs to be managed
Consider using the following script:
```pwsh
$PrincipalID = "<The object ID of the identity here>"
$TopMGID = "<The group ID of the management group here>"
New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $PrincipalID -Scope "/" -RoleDefinitionName "Automation Job Operator"
New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $PrincipalID -Scope "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/$TopMGID" -RoleDefinitionName "Management Group Contributor"
```
The user/principal will also need something like Monitoring Contributor to the Management Group and will also need something like Log Analytics Contributor to the workspace (If they are deploying to the Log Analytics workspace)

issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Description

This applies to all modules, but key-vault is an example

Here's an example:
```bicep
module modKeyvault1 'br/public:avm/res/key-vault/vault:0.9.0' = {
  name: 'keyvault1'
  params: {
    createMode:    <<<<  TRY INTELLISENSE HERE
    softDeleteRetentionInDays: 1         <<<< INVALID VALUE
    name: uniqueString(resourceGroup().id, 'keyvault demo')
  }
}
```
1) Try placing the cursor after "createMode: "
!) no intellisense
EXPECTED: Should provide "default" and "recover" as possible values.  Instead, I had to go to the help page (or deploy to find out the problem).
FIX FOR YOUR MODULE: Use the following code for the param:
```bicep
@description('Optional. The vault\'s create mode to indicate whether the vault need to be recovered or not. - recover or default.')
param createMode 'default' | 'recover' = 'default'
```

2) The above value of softDeleteRetentionInDays is invalid, yet no validation is provided until I deploy
EXPECTED: Should notify me in editor of incorrect value
FIX FOR YOUR MODULE:
```bicep
@description('Optional. softDelete data retention days. It accepts >=7 and <=90.')
@minValue(7)
@maxValue(90)
param softDeleteRetentionInDays int = 90
```

I'm sure there are plenty other examples.  This should be standard expected practice, thanks.

_No response_

issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/db-for-my-sql/flexible-server

### (Optional) Module Version

_No response_

### Description

I’m really looking for is a self-healing mechanism that operates behind the scenes. Specifically, I want the module to avoid errors when I choose the Burstable tier for cost reasons, even though this requires disabling storageAutoGrow. On the other hand, if I select a different tier and want to keep storageAutoGrow enabled, I want everything to function smoothly. storageAutoGrow  must be disabled if Burstable tier is used as it is not supported. 

This is viable for when I am doing code testing or a PoC, because I want to keep cost down as I rip the workload up/down.

My suggestion would be something like this but would need to be verified if it works.
 
```
// Ensure highAvailability is set to 'Disabled' if tier is 'Burstable'
var effectiveHighAvailability = (tier == 'Burstable') ? 'Disabled' : highAvailability

// Ensure storageAutoGrow is disabled if tier is 'Burstable' and highAvailability is 'SameZone' or 'ZoneRedundant'
var effectiveStorageAutoGrow = (tier == 'Burstable' && (highAvailability == 'SameZone' || highAvailability == 'ZoneRedundant')) ? 'Disabled' : storageAutoGrow

var standByAvailabilityZoneTable = {
  Disabled: null
  SameZone: availabilityZone
  ZoneRedundant: highAvailabilityZone
}

var standByAvailabilityZone = standByAvailabilityZoneTable[effectiveHighAvailability]


storageProfile: {
      storageMB: 51200
      backupRetentionDays: 7
      geoRedundantBackup: 'Enabled'
      autoGrow: effectiveStorageAutoGrow
    }
highAvailability: (effectiveHighAvailability != 'Disabled') ? {
      mode: effectiveHighAvailability
      standbyAvailabilityZone: standByAvailabilityZone
    } : null

```

**Self-Healing Mechanism**
**Avoiding Errors:** By conditionally setting `effectiveHighAvailability `and `effectiveStorageAutoGrow`, the code ensures that unsupported configurations (like enabling `storageAutoGrow `with the `Burstable `tier) are automatically adjusted to avoid errors.
**Smooth Functionality:** When a different tier is selected, the code allows storageAutoGrow to be enabled and configures high availability settings appropriately, ensuring smooth operation without manual intervention.
**Behind-the-Scenes Operation:** The use of conditional expressions and mappings allows the module to automatically adjust settings based on the selected parameters, providing a self-healing mechanism that operates transparently to the user.

This approach ensures that the MySQL server configuration is always valid and optimized for the selected tier and high availability settings, preventing errors and maintaining smooth functionality.

comments_list.body:
> Hey [@JPEasier](https://github.com/JPEasier), Please triage this issue when you get the chance 💪

To quote myself, any input would be welcome @JPEasier.

@KLuuKer, I did take a quick look though I can't say that I'm an ACR expect, so please bare with me. 

Regarding the first point, that is, referencing another sub-resource ID you're in good company. Quite a few resource providers unfortunately expect these IDs even though the resources (usually) reside as a sub-resource in the same resource. I guess there may be a few cases where you may want to reference a seperate resource? No clue. Anyhow - you surely know the resource better than me: Is it always the case that a cacheRule would reference a credentialSet on the same resource? If the case, we should be able to 'fix' this for you, by implementing an `existing` resource reference in the cacheRule module. And build the resourceId ourselves. This would still require you to provide the name of the credentialSet, but I guess you'd want to be able to select what set to reference regardless. In the meantime, what I usually did in similar cases was to 'built' the resourceId myself in the parameter file like `'${resourceGroup().id}/providers/Microsoft.(...)'`. Not pretty, but fortunately, these IDs are deterministic.

Regarding the 2nd point it can't really say anything without knowing more about it. From what you described it sounds like the authorization settings come from the registry itself. If the case, we may need to do this implicitely - IF - it's a deterministic behavior. E.g., 'if no `authCredentials` we always fetch them from the containerRegistry' or something like that.

Please let me know what you think 💪  I agree that the module should make using these features as easy as possible (if the price is not making it unmaintainable - of course 😄 )

comments_list.author: jtracey93
comments_list.body:
Hey @kpantos,

Thanks for clarifying 😃 

Just to clarify something around the 4MB limit, this isn't an AVM only thing or a container registry thing for storing modules, it's a hard limit in ARM itself for any one template. And because bicep compiles everything into a single ARM template (JSON file), due to the way it currently is designed and engineered, the 4MB limit can be hit more often in bicep than it did in ARM. As you can see lots of long running discussion on the issue over on the Bicep repository for this (the correct place to vent about the 4MB limit 😁 ) https://github.com/Azure/bicep/issues/5890

@ReneHezser lets get this one on the list for this weeks AVM Bicep core team call and see what we can do, if anything. 

Finally, @kpantos, whilst the template today is just under the limit, what about in the future, being that close means that we could just be kicking the can down the road and the 4MB limit issue will come back for "real" next time you want to add something to the module. Is there any optimisations and reductions you can make to any of the files used to compose the module, e.g. trimming descriptions, removing whitespace, removing duplicated code etc.? (I actually had to do this for an ALZ module, outside of AVM, as we ran into the 4MB limit 😢 )

comments_list.author: kpantos
comments_list.body:
Hey @jtracey93 

I know the 4MB limit is not an AVM thing, and my intention was not to vent about it 😁 but to urge you to bring this up with the ARM team. Leveraging the importance of AVM program and its requirement to have a single deployment - so that it can be re-used, you can put more pressure on the team to increase this limit than me (in this case the ARM team can just argue the use of different deployments).

Also, there are no plans to add anything more to it (unless a new requirement like generating a demo https certificate on the fly arises again 😉). But the pattern's purpose is to provide for a viable, production ready, well architected Azure Container Apps hosting environment (aka LZA) so cutting more stuff from the template would defeat its purpose. The only real alternative would be to pull the pattern down and just use AVM resource modules for the LZA deployment.

Having said that I already went through an optimization cycle since yesterday and now 2 out of 3 tests are passing.  The hub-spoke one though has a dependency in a hub deployment which contains a "heavy" Firewall avm resource module which even with its minimum configuration increases the template file by about 1MB. So, I have two options here, either delete the test all together or provide a way in the pipeline to deploy dependencies in a different deployment (something like a pre-deploy hook?) so that the dependencies template is not added to the pattern module under testing. 

Thoughts?

comments_list.author: jtracey93
comments_list.body:
Hey @kpantos,

No worries, although it did seem like a vit of a vent at AVM 😄 

We have indeed spoken to the ARM/Bicep PG team for this and they are very, very aware of the 4MB limit and they themselves would love to change the limit but its a bit more complicated than a simple increase. Its something they are considering but it wont be anytime soon, so in the meantime we have to deal with it as a known constraint 👍 

Good news on getting 2 out of the 3 tests working. Leave it with us for now, we are meeting as a team tomorrow and will discuss options there and then share back. We don't meet till the afternoon/evening as a JFYI so likely an update on Friday

Thanks for your patience and collaboration here

comments_list.author: JLunda
comments_list.body: Please see my comment here for a workaround that may work in some cases where the files can be minified below the 4 MB request size limit: https://github.com/Azure/bicep/issues/5890#issuecomment-2777578544

comments_list.author: karpikpl
comments_list.body: I think it might be an AVM thing because AVM passes a lot more parameters than standard deployments, not leaving anything to defaults

comments_list.author: karpikpl
comments_list.body:
based on my testing - I only hit 4 MB limit when using AVM - deploying same sets of resources (often more without AVM)
the fact that AVMs pull ton of nested resources, simple DNS zone creation produces 2 MB of JSON, making AVMs unusable in any complex scenario

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
Hey @karpikpl,
it's an ARM/ Bicep issue in that any template, not just AVM, that exceeds the 4MB will fail. You can also hit it completely without using any AVM modules. However, you are right in that AVM modules can, especially if you only use a subset of a module's features, produce a lot of overhead. The DNS Zone example you mentioned is a great showcase in that you would often not deploy every single entry in one go, yet the template contains them all.
I created some docs to target this issue some time ago that can be found here: [Known Issues - 4MB Limitation](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/help-support/known-issues/#4mb-limitation).

The issue becomes even bigger with added features like User-defined types that grealy improve a module's usability, but come at the cost of added size. 

As far as I'm concerned, the underlying issue of the 4MB limit must be solved on a platform level. There is no good way to tackle this from an AVM perspective as its modules would effectively need to be stripped down of every optional feature (e.g., child-resources & extension resources) to keep the size at bay, at which point they don't provide any added value anymore.

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/compute/virtual-machine

### (Optional) Module Version

0.11.0

### Description

I was assisting in a scenario where there was issues getting AVD session hosts enrolled into Intune when deploying them using Bicep.
After testing the Bicep-template being used (which leverages the res/compute/virtual-machine module), I found that the mdmId-property was not specified at the correct location - which is this:

```
    extensionAadJoinConfig: {
        enabled: true
        settings: {
          mdmId: '0000000a-0000-0000-c000-000000000000'
        }
      }
```
 
It was defined like this:

```
    extensionAadJoinConfig: {
        enabled: true
        mdmId: '0000000a-0000-0000-c000-000000000000'    
      }
```
 
The invalid syntax did not produce any errors, but the Intune-enrollment simply didn`t work.

Looking at the documentation for the module, the syntax which was being leveraged seemed correct:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| [`extensionAadJoinConfig`](#parameter-extensionaadjoinconfig) | object | The configuration for the [AAD Join] extension. Must at least contain the ["enabled": true] property to be executed. To enroll in Intune, add the setting mdmId: "0000000a-0000-0000-c000-000000000000". |
 
However, looking at the code for the module, I noticed that the setting needs to be defined inside of a settings-block.

Any thoughts on how we could enhance the user experience?
In addition to updating the documentation, would leveraging user defined types for input validation be an option?

### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/compute/gallery

### (Optional) Module Version

0.8.2

### Description

Similar to https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/issues/3813, the support to define DiskControllerTypes is missing.  
As a result, the VM SKUs that support NVMe cannot be used.

**Azure Portal JSON (VM image definition)**
```
"features": [
            {
                "name": "SecurityType",
                "value": "TrustedLaunchSupported"
            },
            {
                "name": "DiskControllerTypes",
                "value": "SCSI, NVMe"
            }
        ],
```

**BICEP (avm/res/compute/gallery:0.8.2)**
```
    images: [
      {
        name: imagesSharedGalleryName
        identifier: {
          publisher: publisherName
          offer: offerName
          sku: skuVersion
        }
        osType: 'Windows'
        osState: 'Generalized'
        hyperVGeneration: 'V2'
        securityType: 'TrustedLaunch'
        diskcontrollerType: 'NVMe'
      }
    ]
```

> The property "diskcontrollerType" is not allowed on objects of type "{ name: string, description: null | string, osType: 'Linux' | 'Windows', osState: 'Generalized' | 'Specialized', identifier: identifierType, vCPUs: resourceRangeType, memory: resourceRangeType, hyperVGeneration: 'V1' | 'V2' | null, securityType: 'ConfidentialVM' | 'ConfidentialVMSupported' | 'Standard' | 'TrustedLaunch' | 'TrustedLaunchAndConfidentialVmSupported' | 'TrustedLaunchSupported' | null, isAcceleratedNetworkSupported: bool | null, isHibernateSupported: bool | null, architecture: 'Arm64' | 'x64' | null, eula: null | string, privacyStatementUri: null | string, releaseNoteUri: null | string, purchasePlan: purchasePlanType, endOfLife: null | string, excludedDiskTypes: null | string[] }". Permissible properties include "architecture", "description", "endOfLife", "eula", "excludedDiskTypes", "isAcceleratedNetworkSupported", "isHibernateSupported", "memory", "privacyStatementUri", "purchasePlan", "releaseNoteUri", "vCPUs".bicep[BCP037](https://aka.ms/bicep/core-diagnostics#BCP037)


### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues
### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/container-service/managed-cluster

### (Optional) Module Version

0.8.0

### Description

## Issue Summary

When deploying the AKS cluster, Prometheus is enabled by default. However, upon accessing the Azure portal, I encounter the following error message:
> You do not have access to the associated data collection rule to view the Azure Monitor workspace or the data collection rule has been deleted. Reconfigure

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df70484c-5077-40de-9cbb-af79042e7073)

## Steps to Reproduce:

Deploy AKS with bicep parameters I use to deploy monitoring  for the aks cluster: 

    enableContainerInsights: true
    enableAzureMonitorProfileMetrics: true
    metricLabelsAllowlist: 'nodes=[*], pods=[*]'


Am I missing something in my configuration? I cannot find any data collection rule that should be created.


### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

issues.author: anderseide
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/ptn/dev-ops/cicd-agents-and-runners

### (Optional) Module Version

_No response_

### Description

The following features would be nice to have in the module

* Possibility to configure additional environment variables on Container Instances and Container Apps resource
* Possibility to configure custom runner images
* Possibility to use existing Log Analytics Workspace
* Possibility to use existing Azure Container Registry
* Make githubRepository parameter optional (for organization scope deployment of runner)
* Add support for Managed DevOps pools: `avm/res/dev-ops-infrastructure/pool`
* Add Azure Firewall as an optional configuration to align module towards Well-Architected Framework

When networkType: 'createNew'
* (Would be nice) Use cdir function to configure subnets based on addressSpace parameter instead of hard coded subnet size as default (makes the deployment fail if subnet configuration is missing from networkConfiguration)
* Enable/disable if private DNS zones should be deployed or not.

I'd like to add features from this module proposal to the list: https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Verified-Modules/issues/1878
- Docker image creation
  - Bring your own dockerfile, or use the default dockerfile
  - Bring your own entrypoint shell script, or use the default entrypoint
  - Rebuild the container image on a schedule, and purge old images from the container registry


### (Optional) Correlation Id

issues.author: monikanagy
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/web/static-site

### (Optional) Module Version

_No response_

### Description

The issue is opened for Static Web App because that is where I have noticed and tested it, but the same bug seems to exist in multiple templates:
- avm/res/app-configuration/configuration-store
- avm/res/compute/dis-encryption-set
- avm/res/document-db/database-account
- avm/res/machine-learning-services/workspace/compute
- avm/res/search/search-service
- avm/res/signal-r-service/signal-r
- avm/res/sql/managed-instance
- avm/res/sql/server
- avm/res/web/hosting-environment - ([Microsoft.Web/hostingEnvironments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.web/hostingenvironments?pivots=deployment-language-bicep) does not support the identity property, so should be removed I believe)
- avm/res/web/static-site

I would like to request the fix of all bugs in this request - hope that I do not need to open an issue for each module separately.

#### Describe the bug
When deploying the template with system-assigned managed identity explicitly set to false while not providing any user-assigned managed resource id, the deployment validation fails.

#### Error message 
New-AzResourceGroupDeployment: 10:09:05 - Error: Code=InvalidTemplate; Message=Deployment template parse failed: 'Required property 'type' expects a value but got null. Path ''.'.

The search/search-service gives a different error:
New-AzResourceGroupDeployment: 10:09:05 - Error: Code=InvalidTemplate; Message=Deployment template parse failed: 'Error converting value "" to type 'Azure.Deployments.Core.Definitions.Resources.ResourceIdentityType'. Path 'type'.'.

#### To Reproduce
Create deployment invoking the module as below. 
```bicep
module staticwebapp 'br/public:avm/res/web/static-site:0.8.2' = {
  name: 'deploy-static-webapp'
  params: {
    name: 'nmfstaticwebapp'
    managedIdentities: {
      systemAssigned: false
      userAssignedResourceIds: []
    }
  }
}
```

#### Root cause and suggested fix
The `identity` property accepts only the following values: `'None' | 'SystemAssigned' | 'SystemAssigned, UserAssigned' | 'UserAssigned'` .

The bicep code in mentioned modules sets the type to `null` or `''` instead of None at the following section:
```bicep
var identity = !empty(managedIdentities)
  ? {
      type: (managedIdentities.?systemAssigned ?? false)
        ? (!empty(managedIdentities.?userAssignedResourceIds ?? {}) ? 'SystemAssigned, UserAssigned' : 'SystemAssigned')
        : (!empty(managedIdentities.?userAssignedResourceIds ?? {}) ? 'UserAssigned' : null)
      userAssignedIdentities: !empty(formattedUserAssignedIdentities) ? formattedUserAssignedIdentities : null
    }
  : null
```

This can be adjusted to the below to resolve the bug (already implemented the same way in multiple templates, e.g. data-factory/factory).
```bicep
var identity = !empty(managedIdentities)
  ? {
      type: (managedIdentities.?systemAssigned ?? false)
        ? (!empty(managedIdentities.?userAssignedResourceIds ?? {}) ? 'SystemAssigned, UserAssigned' : 'SystemAssigned')
        : (!empty(managedIdentities.?userAssignedResourceIds ?? {}) ? 'UserAssigned' : 'None')
      userAssignedIdentities: !empty(formattedUserAssignedIdentities) ? formattedUserAssignedIdentities : null
    }
  : null
```

#### Additional context
This is not a blocking issue because the desired result can be achieved by simply leaving the the managedIdentities parameter out of the deployment. This might lower the priority to fix it, but should happen regardless.

### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

issues.author: paul-towler
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/ptn/authorization/policy-assignment

### (Optional) Module Version

0.3.1

### Description

When a User-Assigned Identity is used for a Policy Assignment, the required Role Definition IDs are not applied.

I have identified the issue with the sub-modules:
 - modules/management-group.bicep
 - modules/subscription.bicep
 - modules/resource-group.bicep

Each module has several issues preventing User Assigned Identities from receiving the appropriate role assignments.   I'll highlight them all later in this post, but the main issue is the `additional-rbac-asi-def-loop` modules defined to apply role assignments to the targeted resource type. Each module validates three conditions to execute. The last condition is if the identity is `SystemAssigned`. This means all 'UserAssigned' Identities are ignored.

For example:

``` bicep
module managementGroupRoleAssignments 'management-group-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep' = [
  for roleDefinitionId in roleDefinitionIds: if (!empty(roleDefinitionIds) && !empty(additionalManagementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo) && identity == 'SystemAssigned') { // <---- This is the main issue
    name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location, roleDefinitionId, name)}-PolicyAssignment-MG-Module-Additional-RBAC'
    params: {
      name: name
      policyAssignmentIdentityId: policyAssignment.identity.principalId
      roleDefinitionId: roleDefinitionId
      managementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo: finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo
    }
  }
]
```

To correct all issues, please refer to the following:

1. Update the main module (main.bicep)

   Change the `userAssignedIdentityId` param for each policyAssignment module to `userAssignedIdentity` and include the resourceId and principalId. For example:
    
    ``` bicep
    userAssignedIdentityId: userAssignedIdentityId
    ```
    to

    ``` bicep
    userAssignedIdentity: userAssignedIdentity // must contain resouceId and principalId
    ```

2.  Change userAssignedIdentityId
     
     The parameter userAssignedIdentityId needs to change from a string to an object. This allows the resourceId and principalId to be referenced by the modules and the `identityVar` variable. For example:

    ``` bicep
    param userAssignedIdentityId string = ''
    ```
    to

    ``` bicep
    param userAssignedIdentity object = {}
    ```
   
3. Update identityVar variable.
    
    Update 'identityVar' variable to accommodate the change to the `userAssignedIdentity`  parameter. For example:

    ``` bicep
    var identityVar = identity == 'SystemAssigned'
      ? {
           type: identity
         }
      : identity == 'UserAssigned'
        ? {
             type: identity
             userAssignedIdentities: {
               '${userAssignedIdentityId}': {}
             }
           }
         : null
    ```
    to

    ``` bicep
    var identityVar = identity == 'SystemAssigned'
      ? {
           type: identity
         }
      : identity == 'UserAssigned'
        ? {
             type: identity
             userAssignedIdentities: {
               '${userAssignedIdentity.resourceId}': {}
             }
           }
         : null
    ```

4. Update finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo variable

    Remove the condition for `SystemAssigned` Identity. `UserAssigned' Idenities are ignored.

     ``` bicep
    var finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo = identity == 'SystemAssigned'
      ? union(additionalManagementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo, [managementGroup().name])
      : []
    ```
    to

    ``` bicep
    var finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo = union(additionalManagementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo, [managementGroup().name])
    ```

5. Update management-group-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep module

   Remove `&& identity == 'SystemAssigned'` from the condition, replace `additionalManagementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo` with `finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo` and update the reference to the `policyAssignmentIdentityId`. For example:

     ``` bicep
    module managementGroupRoleAssignments 'management-group-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep' = [
      for roleDefinitionId in roleDefinitionIds: if (!empty(roleDefinitionIds) && !empty(additionalManagementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo) && identity == 'SystemAssigned') {
        name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location, roleDefinitionId, name)}-PolicyAssignment-MG-Module-Additional-RBAC'
        params: {
          name: name
          policyAssignmentIdentityId: policyAssignment.identity.principalId
          roleDefinitionId: roleDefinitionId
          managementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo: finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo
        }
      }
    ]
    ```
    to

     ``` bicep
    module managementGroupRoleAssignments 'management-group-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep' = [
      for roleDefinitionId in roleDefinitionIds: if (!empty(roleDefinitionIds) && !empty(finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo)) {
        name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location, roleDefinitionId, name)}-PolicyAssignment-MG-Module-Additional-RBAC'
        params: {
          name: name
          policyAssignmentIdentityId: identity == 'SystemAssigned' ? policyAssignment.identity.principalId : userAssignedIdentity.principalId
          roleDefinitionId: roleDefinitionId
          managementGroupsIDsToAssignRbacTo: finalArrayOfManagementGroupsToAssignRbacTo
        }
      }
    ]

6. Update Subscription and Resource Group additional-rbac-asi-def-loop  modules

   Remove `&& identity == 'SystemAssigned'` from the condition, and update the reference to the `policyAssignmentIdentityId`. For example:

     ``` bicep
    module additionalSubscriptionRoleAssignments 'subscription-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep' = [
      for roleDefinitionId in roleDefinitionIds: if (!empty(roleDefinitionIds) && !empty(additionalSubscriptionIDsToAssignRbacTo) && identity == 'SystemAssigned') {
        name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location, roleDefinitionId, name)}-PolicyAssignment-MG-Module-Additional-RBAC-Subs'
        params: {
          name: name
          policyAssignmentIdentityId: policyAssignment.identity.principalId
          roleDefinitionId: roleDefinitionId
          subscriptionIDsToAssignRbacTo: additionalSubscriptionIDsToAssignRbacTo
        }
      }
    ]

    module additionalResourceGroupRoleAssignments 'resource-group-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep' = [
      for roleDefinitionId in roleDefinitionIds: if (!empty(roleDefinitionIds) && !empty(additionalResourceGroupResourceIDsToAssignRbacTo) && identity == 'SystemAssigned') {
        name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location, roleDefinitionId, name)}-PolicyAssignment-MG-Module-Additional-RBAC-RGs'
        params: {
          name: name
          policyAssignmentIdentityId: policyAssignment.identity.principalId
          roleDefinitionId: roleDefinitionId
          resourceGroupResourceIDsToAssignRbacTo: additionalResourceGroupResourceIDsToAssignRbacTo
        }
      }
    ]
    ```
    to

     ``` bicep
    module additionalSubscriptionRoleAssignments 'subscription-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep' = [
      for roleDefinitionId in roleDefinitionIds: if (!empty(roleDefinitionIds) && !empty(additionalSubscriptionIDsToAssignRbacTo)) {
        name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location, roleDefinitionId, name)}-PolicyAssignment-MG-Module-Additional-RBAC-Subs'
        params: {
          name: name
          policyAssignmentIdentityId: identity == 'SystemAssigned' ? policyAssignment.identity.principalId : userAssignedIdentity.principalId
          roleDefinitionId: roleDefinitionId
          subscriptionIDsToAssignRbacTo: additionalSubscriptionIDsToAssignRbacTo
        }
      }
    ]

    module additionalResourceGroupRoleAssignments 'resource-group-additional-rbac-asi-def-loop.bicep' = [
      for roleDefinitionId in roleDefinitionIds: if (!empty(roleDefinitionIds) && !empty(additionalResourceGroupResourceIDsToAssignRbacTo)) {
        name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location, roleDefinitionId, name)}-PolicyAssignment-MG-Module-Additional-RBAC-RGs'
        params: {
          name: name

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/ptn/lz/sub-vending

### (Optional) Module Version

0.3

### Description

**Scenario:** Many of our Customers work sensitive environments in which giving tenant root permissions is not acceptable. To overcome this the default Management Group for new subscription is changed in the Azure Tenant Settings. Customers spin up a 'commissioning' management group on the same level as the intermediate root and use this as the target management group for the new subscriptions, this prevents permissions being needed at the tenant root group and means that SCF & SCF Policies (These are deployed by Microsoft Employees in projects with complex customer) are compliant.

**Issue:** When creating a subscription in complex environments, not all custom roles will be assignable at the scope the subscription is created (Commissioning MG as above or Tenant Root). Therefore deployments will fail if you want to target a custom role

**Possible Fix:** Enable a customRolesAssignment block to take action **after** the subscription has been moved to the landing zone. Therefore, enabling and expediting the process of ownership for application teams that are using the Landing Zones.

### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/fabric/capacity

### (Optional) Module Version

0.1.1

### Description

I am working with some Fabric Capacities that are sometimes in a paused state to reduce costs. It is my understanding that when using a Pay-As-You-Go capacity, this is common to ensure the business reduces costs.
However, if an ADO pipeline runs with Bicep calling this AVM module and tries to change the SKU from one type to another (example: F2 --> F4) then the deployment will fail as the resource is not in a ready state with the following error:
```
"code": "BadRequest",
"message": "Service is not ready to be updated"
```
It is my understanding that the rule is that Bicep is declarative and states the end-result of the resource regardless of how you got there. In that case, it would make sense to possibly resolve this by:

- Find a way to allow the change of F SKU while the capacity is paused (this seems to me to be the easiest path as it is a config change) 
- Find the current state and store it. If paused, then start the capacity, change the SKU, and set the state to the previous value. Otherwise, just change the SKU.
- Provide an additional parameter that allows the caller to decide whether to allow the starting of the capacity to allow changes. That allows for no change to current users to have no change in functionality (this failure if paused) but allow anyone to override that behavior to allow the capacity to be started and stopped to make the change. I do not see any reason for someone ever **not** allow that change, but if needed, then this boolean would allow for that. Since this is version 0.1.1 I do not see this as a large breaking change.

Currently, automation would intermittently fail because of the current state instead of allowing the change and ensuring the resource ends up in the state described in Bicep.

### (Optional) Correlation Id

d0d6a4fe-7fce-442d-bfd0-a564b76713e8

Hey @JoelMiller74,
the original owner, @hundredacres assigned Co-Pilot to a wide range of issues at the time that then unfortunately sat stale. Presumably because it became pretty quickly pretty apparent that CoPilot may offer a solution but is unable to validate the changes and requires manual support to get PRs through the finish line. I had a quick look at the link PR and, well, it's what I essentially worte in my comment above. It's deploying additional resources (most notably a managed identity + deployment script) to execute custom logic inside the module to work around the issue. This adds not only a massive amount of complexity but also will absolutely break deployments in environments where e.g. private networking is enforced (which would require e.g., a custom storage account and vnet injection for the deployment script, not to mention a potential cleanup logic). 

Instead of merging that, I'd really appreciate if somebody knowledgable of the service, e.g., @mswantek68 / @cmaneu  (the current owners) to share their thoughts as I'm pretty sure the better path would be to get the actual issue fixed by the RP (if there's one) instead of introducing a complex workaround that may likely break other deployments in turn.

So much for the CoPilot PR. This does **not** excuse that this issue laid dormant for so long and should long have been tackled ☝️ The same issue you describe also applies to e.g., the Azure Data Explorer btw. Used that one at a customer and it also shut down automatically if there was no activity for some time, rendering subsequent (in that case Terraform) deployments impossible. Here is the code. This is simplified and stripped down. Just an ADO YAML pipeline calling the task: AzureResourceManagerTemplateDeployment@3, a main.bicep file calling the AVM Module with SkuName parameter, and a main-qa.bicepparam that passes in the SKU: F2, F4, F8, etc...

Hopefully I did not strip out too much but there was not a lot more to it. For Fabic Capacity, we really only have a capacity name, SKU, and a list of admins. Almost everything else is managed differently within Fabric. This is the only part using Azure, Bicep, ADO.

# azure-pipelines.yml

```yml
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
    - main

variables:
  azureResourceManagerConnectionQA: 'asc-bicep-qa'

type configType =

  | webConfigType
```

It just feels weird to import them from `avm/res/web/site/slot` instead of `avm/res/web/site/config`

-------

More comments about `avm/res/web/site/config`

I think it has some logic flaws:

* allowed values on name parameter suggests it can be used to setup any `Microsoft.Web/sites/config` resource but `currentAppSettings` is for simple property bag with string values
* should it be splitted into two modules: one for appsettings with logic and other for remaining config types

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
> First comment: Should `br/public:avm/res/web/site/config` export types?
> 
> Now I can build exact typing for our use case. E.g.
> 
> import { 
>   basicPublishingCredentialsPolicyType
>   authSettingsV2ConfigType
>   webConfigType
>  } from 'br/public:avm/res/web/site/slot:0.1.0'
> 
> @description('The type of a site configuration.')
> @discriminator('name')
> type configType =
>   | authSettingsV2ConfigType
>   | webConfigType
> It just feels weird to import them from `avm/res/web/site/slot` instead of `avm/res/web/site/config`
> 
> More comments about `avm/res/web/site/config`
> 
> I think it has some logic flaws:
> 
> * allowed values on name parameter suggests it can be used to setup any `Microsoft.Web/sites/config` resource but `currentAppSettings` is for simple property bag with string values
> * should it be splitted into two modules: one for appsettings with logic and other for remaining config types

Thanks for your comments. To share some thoughts
- Regarding # 1: I agree and am not suprised. The reason it's in the slot comes down to avoiding duplication. Technically speaking, each slot is almost 1:1 the same as the parent resource. As such, both provide the same config properties at different scopes. If we were to implement the type in the `web/site` (not the `config` itself as it its name is the key for the `properties` variants too, making them unusuable in the `config` module itself). Now, we could've either implemented the type twice (which would be 1.300 lines of code duplicated), or (and that's what we ended up doing), implement it at the lowest level and import it again at the higher ones. The big downside is the uninuitiveness, but the alternative is subjectively much worse. The good news is that the PG may implement a feature that allows us not export imported types. So the `web/site` module could import the types from the `web/sites/slot` module and make it available again. As such it would hopefully make it more intuitive as it is right now
-  Regarding # 2: The `currentAppSettings` would be merged together with whatever other configs you'd specify. If it's not there, the config would always overwrite all settings. We used to have issue to specifically not do that and preserve the values. Naturally, it makes more sense from the angle of the calling module (e.g., the slot module that fetches those settings and passes them to the config).
  Splitting could be done but only by nesting one part in a nested module of the other (i.e., in a nested `/modules/` folder). 2 modules on the same level would break the resource provider hierachy.

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
Hey @audhage,
thank you for your issue. That was actually something that was debated a few times in the past with the outcome that we settled with something akin to 'top level properties should have their own parameter, anything nested can be part of a UDT/RDT-typed object parameter'.
The problem with moving more parameters into a single type is rooted in the limitations of the same. E.g.,  we cannot define defaults for individual parameters of a type, but only for the entire typed object itself. I'd also argue that it makes the template itself a lot more complex as we usually loop through and modify quite a few parameters - and a top-level type means we'd need to dig quite a lot into x-levels of nesting for pretty much everything we want to do (be it using a value or referncing it).
There also used to be a point of 'parameters allow for more validation than types' (e.g., min/max/allowedValues/etc.), but I think that's actually not true anymore, so nevermind that 😄 

All that said, I don't want to imply your ask does not make sense. If get where you're comming from. To improve the module usability for almost the purpose you're referring to, we did define a recommendation somewhere to please add the `@export()` annotation to any custom type - especially for top-level parameters, to help users that want to re-use set types in their patterns to import them exactly in the way you described.

Maybe some of the other (technical) maintainers also want to add their thoughts, cc: @Azure/avm-core-team-technical-bicep

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/compute/disk

### (Optional) Module Version

_No response_

### Description

### Description

When deploying virtual machines with `securityType = 'ConfidentialVM'` using the [`avm/res/compute/virtual-machine`](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/tree/main/avm/res/compute/virtual-machine) module, the deployment fails due to a missing required property:

> `Required parameter for Confidential VMs 'managedDisk.securityProfile.securityEncryptionType' is missing (null).`

This is because the `securityEncryptionType` must be explicitly set under `osDisk.securityProfile` when using Confidential VMs. However, the current AVM module does not expose or forward this property, making Confidential VM deployments impossible without forking the module.

### Expected Enhancement

Please extend the module to support the following structure within `osDisk`:

```bicep
osDisk: {
  ...
  securityProfile: {
    securityEncryptionType: 'DiskWithVMGuestState' // or 'VMGuestStateOnly'
  }
}
```

### Use Case

Customers adopting Confidential VMs (e.g., DCsv5-series) need this setting to meet platform requirements. Without this enhancement, the AVM module cannot be used for secure workloads or policy-driven deployments that require Confidential Compute.

In our case, we are deploying AVD session hosts using `securityType = 'ConfidentialVM'`. Without the `securityEncryptionType` field, deployment fails.

2412

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/compute/virtual-machine

### (Optional) Module Version

0.16

### Description

Azure Virtual Machines (VMs) using the `'ConfidentialVM'` `securityType` require both `secureBootEnabled` and `vTpmEnabled` parameters to be set to `true` for a VM's `uefiSettings`.

Currently, this is only possible for VMs with `securityType` `'TrustedLaunch'`, see reference:

https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/blob/b82aee5cc4bd0f8ca9097db802b8baf3d1bd6320/avm/res/compute/virtual-machine/main.bicep#L561-L567

A change must be applied to enable the creation of VMs with the `'ConfidentialVM'` `securityType` with both `secureBootEnabled` and `vTpmEnabled` set to `true` for the VM's `uefiSettings`, e.g.

```
uefiSettings: (securityType == 'TrustedLaunch' || securityType == 'ConfidentialVM')
  ? {
      secureBootEnabled: secureBootEnabled
      vTpmEnabled: vTpmEnabled
    }
  : null
}
```

comments_list.author: picccard
comments_list.body:
Hi, it is possible to set `criterionType: 'DynamicThresholdCriterion'` when the criteria odata type is `Microsoft.Azure.Monitor.MultipleResourceMultipleMetricCriteria`. Creating the alert in the portal first and exporting it as bicep helps to get a feel for the properties 👍 


```bicep
targetScope = 'resourceGroup'

var webAppToMonitor = '/subscriptions/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789876/resourceGroups/rg-demo-001/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/app-demo-001'

module dynamicAlertDemo 'br/public:avm/res/insights/metric-alert:0.4.0' = {
  params: {
    name: 'demo-alert-dynamic-001'
    severity: 3
    enabled: true
    scopes: [webAppToMonitor]
    evaluationFrequency: 'PT1M'
    windowSize: 'PT5M'
    criteria: {
      'odata.type': 'Microsoft.Azure.Monitor.MultipleResourceMultipleMetricCriteria'
      allof: [
        {
          alertSensitivity: 'Medium'
          failingPeriods: {
            numberOfEvaluationPeriods: 4
            minFailingPeriodsToAlert: 4
          }
          name: 'Metric1'
          metricNamespace: 'Microsoft.Web/sites'
          metricName: 'HttpResponseTime'
          operator: 'GreaterOrLessThan'
          timeAggregation: 'Average'
          skipMetricValidation: false
          criterionType: 'DynamicThresholdCriterion'
        }
      ]
    }
    autoMitigate: true
    targetResourceRegion: 'eastus'
    targetResourceType: 'Microsoft.Web/sites'
  }
}
```

comments_list.author: Prajwal-Microsoft
comments_list.body:
@AlexanderSehr , @sethsteenken ,

We had raised a support ticket with Azure and they have given below suggestions, however we can't control these as it is something which needs to be handled with in AVM module. If you have any workaround for this issue please let us know.

Root Cause
ARM locks private endpoint sub-resources (NIC, Private Link Service connection, DNS zone group) for the duration of background provisioning tasks. Although the initial deployment reports Succeeded, some asynchronous operations remain in progress. A subsequent deployment attempt then collides with those locks and returns AnotherOperationInProgress. This behavior is expected for network resources without explicit sequencing or a pause between deployments.

Solution Steps
Azure Portal

In the Azure Portal, go to Resource groups > rg-cawafavmts123 > Deployments.

Select the failed deployment (e.g., avm.res.sql.server.sqldb-cawafavmts123snegq), then open Operations.

Verify no operations are in Running or InProgress state. Wait until all operations complete.

Navigate to the Private Endpoint resource and confirm Provisioning state is Succeeded.

Azure CLI

Check for any in-progress operations:

```pwsh
az deployment group operation list \
  --resource-group rg-cawafavmts123 \
  --name avm.res.sql.server.sqldb-cawafavmts123snegq \
  --query "[?properties.provisioningState=='Running']"
```

Wait until this returns an empty array.

Redeploy your Bicep template:

```pwsh
az deployment group create \
  --resource-group rg-cawafavmts123 \
  --template-file main.bicep \
  --parameters .json \
  --mode Incremental
```

Update Bicep to enforce ordering:

```bicep
resource sqlServer 'Microsoft.Sql/servers@2022-02-01-preview' = {
  name: sqlServerName
  location: location
  // …
}

resource privateEndpoint 'Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints@2021-05-01' = {
  name: '${sqlServerName}-pe'
  location: resourceGroup().location
  properties: {
    // …
  }
  dependsOn: [
    sqlServer
    virtualNetwork  // reference to your VNet resource
    subnet          // reference to your Subnet resource
  ]
}
```

If you use a module for the private endpoint, pass dependsOn to the module call:

```bicep
module peModule 'privateEndpointModule.bicep' = {
  name: 'sqlPrivateEndpoint'
  params: { /* … */ }
  dependsOn: [
    sqlServer
    networkModule
  ]
}
```

Add a brief pause in your CI/CD pipeline before redeploying:

Azure DevOps YAML:

```yaml
- script: |
    echo "Pausing 180s for private endpoint propagation..."
    sleep 180
  displayName: 'Wait for ARM locks to clear'
``` 

Additional Information
Best practice is to declare explicit dependsOn for all network resources in Bicep to enforce proper sequencing.

Introducing a short delay (2–5 minutes) or implementing retry logic for the Private Endpoint deployment mitigates transient lock conflicts.

Reference on Private Endpoint ARM templates and dependencies:

[https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/private-link/create-private-endpoint-template](https://nam06.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Flearn.microsoft.com%2Fazure%2Fprivate-link%2Fcreate-private-endpoint-template&data=05%7C02%7Cv-dcprajwal%40microsoft.com%7C13822451950644d1197908de318b1e11%7C72f988bf86f141af91ab2d7cd011db47%7C1%7C0%7C639002670874640150%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=PxvzXM2Twj1j3RpH2EMexYuSvoO5HFtuecthUNStK8E%3D&reserved=0)

Monitor Azure Service Health for any ongoing Private Link incidents in All regions: 

[https://status.azure.com](https://nam06.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstatus.azure.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cv-dcprajwal%40microsoft.com%7C13822451950644d1197908de318b1e11%7C72f988bf86f141af91ab2d7cd011db47%7C1%7C0%7C639002670874670200%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=7sr4Gab3U4zkrswgKR5FqnSX%2BFAgtdkC%2FF4FoeKDpts%3D&reserved=0)

comments_list.author: Prajwal-Microsoft
AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
@Prajwal-Microsoft, thank you very much for the extensive input. 
For the last example, I have the wild guess the later deployment may take a few seconds longer to start (as it's yet another deployment which waits until the entire first deployment is done) and hence does not have the issue.

As per what you described above and have gotten back from the PG, I think this would be a very good case for the upcoming [waitandretry()](https://github.com/Azure/bicep/blob/main/docs/experimental-features.md#waitandretry) feature which is currently experimental. Upon failing a deployment it would wait for a short period, try again, if it fails again, wait a bit longer, etc. etc.
AVM module-wise this makes the most sense to me as impementing anything custom would mean to deploy e.g. a deployent script with a custom wait logic (which would be an overkill) or enforce a wait some other way via dummy-deployments - which is really not a good practice.

Other than that, only a `batchSize()` would've come to mind. But as it appears the issue also appears for individual PEs, yet alone multiple it may not help here.

br/public:avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set:0.8.1

### Description

I'm trying to configure the health probe to use "Binary Health Check" for a virtual machine scale set. In order to do this I set the typeHandlerVersion to 1.0 in order to set the binary health check as opposed to the "Rich health Check" 

To do this my "extensionHealthConfig" config looks like this:

```bicep
extensionHealthConfig: {
      typeHandlerVersion: '1.0'
      enabled: true
      protocol:'http'
      port: <PORT>
      requestPath: '/api/health' 
      intervalInSeconds: 30
      numberOfProbes: 3
}
``` 

This results in the heath check config applied to the VMSS having a gracePeriod applied to it. Which is invalid for the Binary Heath Check configuration resulting in the following error when attempting to provision the VMSS

```json
{   "code": "VMExtensionProvisioningError",   "target": "42",   "message": "VM has reported a failure when processing extension 'HealthExtension' (publisher 'Microsoft.ManagedServices' and type 'ApplicationHealthLinux'). Error message: 'Enable failed: failed to get configuration: json validation error: invalid public settings JSON: gracePeriod: Additional property gracePeriod is not allowed'. More information on troubleshooting is available at https://aka.ms/vmextensionlinuxtroubleshoot. " }
```

This is due to how the settings are applied to the heath check inside the main.bicep at L578 where the Grace Period is set even if the extensionHealthConfig.?typeHandlerVersion is version 1.0. resulting in the invalid configuration for "Binary Health Checks"

Expected Behaviour: 

When setting the typeHandlerVersion to 1.0 the resultant health probe settings should not include the gracePeriod.

issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Description

I spent a few hours troubleshooting why Cloud-init wasn’t working for the [AVM VMSS Module ](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/tree/main/avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set). Found out that this module already Base64 encodes and that unlike the API, it doesn’t need you to add `customData: loadContentAsBase64('user-data.yaml') `, but you still need to add `customData: loadTextContent('user-data.yaml') `.  

I do believe this needs to be documented better with correct examples. I understand the documentation states “[Base64 encoding is done automatically](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/tree/main/avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set#parameter-customdata)”, but did stop me from double encoding it myself and then after troubleshooting found out that was the issue. Then I found another way to encode it and then had malformed data as it was using the wrong base64 encryption. Definitely could be solved with an example for future clarity. 

Please do share the correct method to avoid others having this issue. Correct method is `customData: loadTextContent('cloud-init.yaml') ` or `param cloudinit string = loadTextContent('cloud-init.yaml `. Would also be helpful to link people to the [cloudinit troubleshooting  ](https://cloudinit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/howto/debugging.html) as this helped understand the issues.

comments_list.author: JulioGPena
comments_list.body:
We hit a slightly different variant of this bug in our deployment pipeline.

Scenario: We have an existing CosmosDB MongoDB account that was originally provisioned without database-level throughput (i.e., per-collection dedicated throughput model). All 9 of our collections each own their own autoscale RU allocation. The database resource itself has no options set, which is what CosmosDB requires for the per-collection model.

What happened: After moving to the AVM module (avm/res/document-db/database-account:0.19.0) and passing our database via mongodbDatabases, the sub-module's hard-coded param throughput int = 400 caused the redeployment to attempt setting options: { throughput: 400 } on an already-existing database that was created in per-collection mode.

Result: Deployment failed with 'Cannot set throughput for database that is not created with throughput'.

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body: ping @cmaneu

comments_list.author: JulioGPena
comments_list.body:
There was yet another 'facet' of this error that we encountered.

As a workaround to the shared above, we split the deployment (AVM for the account + manual Bicep resource for the database), but this introduced a second issue: the module incorrectly infers the database kind (defaulting to GlobalDocumentDB instead of respecting capabilities like EnableMongo) when no database is set, which breaks fresh deployments. Took some time to notice cause it seems that this is a problem only with fresh deployments, when the account already exists it succeeds.

I was able to recreate it via AVM deployment. Went ahead in the portal and upgraded to the Standard tier. Took the ARM template from that and deleted the AVM deployed resource.

>

Hola @JFolberth,

may it not be as 'simpel' as this line

https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/blob/9574e2e3b140bfbfa2b504e6bc36e83c12d6fec9/avm/res/app-configuration/configuration-store/main.bicep#L217


being the culpit? As per @OlehGap's description, upon the first deployment using the `Developer` SKU, this setting would be configured with 0, no matter what you do. If you then switch it to anything but `Developer` or `Free`, the configuration 'suddenly' applies with a value of `7` (as per the example).
So, in that case I'd argue the error message makes sense as the template tries to indeed change the value. @OlehGap, just for fun, could you try and deploy the module using the `Standard` SKU, and `0` being configured for the `softDeleteRetentionInDays`? My guess is that this will pass.

If the case, I'd argue we should change the implamentation @JFolberth. I see two options here. Either
- We change the implementation so that `null` is passed to the RP instead of 0 - assuming the RP accepts that. - OR
- We change it to 
   ```bicep
   ...(sku != 'Free' && sku != 'Developer'
     ? {
         softDeleteRetentionInDays: softDeleteRetentionInDays
       }
     : {})
   ```
   which means no value is passed to the API endpoint if the condition does not apply.

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Description

Example: [ref](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/6335/commits/0643080b1ae5717ff287f5b07157648988ebd961)

We could get started with inline comments and retrospectively match comments from the test file to the inline parameter name in the usage examples.
For full-on comment blocks on top of parameters it would be more complicated as we'd need to match it with whatever next parameter name below it. This has the additional complication that contributors may have used the comment to e.g., group a section of the test file which won't carry over into the sorted param block in the readme.

PS: The parameters are sorted so that the result is deteministic. Without, different systems may convert the parameter block to differntly-sorted JSON blocks and hence fail the static tests. It may be possible to ignore this if we don't use JSON as the basis anymore (i.e., fully depend on interpreting Bicep). E.g. either by only using the JSON for the JSON-parameter example, or removing it entirely.

issues.author: ericscheffler
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Description

I have my AVM CI/CD environment configured to use an internal Azure subscription; there are Azure policies that will prevent deployment of Storage Accounts with public access, and Event Hub Namespaces without Local Authentication disabled:

- Storage Account - Requires either publicNetworkAccess disabled or a skip tag
- Event Hub Namespace - Requires disableLocalAuth set to true or a skip tag

To work around this the policy managers have enabled the use of skip tags; Azure tags with specific values can be added to resources to allow them to be deployed normally. The problem is that  diagnostic.dependencies.bicep does not have the tags parameter exposed, so the necessary skip tags can't be added to allow my tests to complete without being impeded by policy. 

Propose the following:

- Add the 'tags' parameter to the resources defined in diagnostic.dependencies.bicep, and expose the parameter as an input
- Consider disabling public access for these resources altogether if not needed for any other patterns or resources
- API updates as appropriate

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
Hey @ericscheffler,
Thanks for the issue. @eriqua please also take a look at this when you have the chance. Eric and I already chatted about it in the last few weeks. 🙂

comments_list.author: eriqua
comments_list.body:
@ericscheffler @AlexanderSehr I wouldn't see any problem in exposing tags. I believe this would cover already, likely the easiest fix and I'd tend to start with that. 
In a second stage, even extend the same to all dependencies for the same reason. For example, I'd expect dependency subnets not having nsg could be an issue for test environments protected by policies.
As per disabling public access I guess this would come together with adding private endpoints, so maybe we can discuss this a little further. Dependencies are usually implemented as minimum required resources, we also skip psrule on those as the primary goal of the test is to validate the primary resource. I believe adding tags can be a good trade off.
The only downside we faced with tags is they contribute to the number of write operations, increasing the chance of throttling. In our case I don't expect them to have an impact in this sense though.

comments_list.author: ericscheffler
comments_list.body:
@eriqua 
> For example, I'd expect dependency subnets not having nsg could be an issue for test environments protected by policies

This is a great example; there are other policies internally about disabling default outbound access for subnets (aka, Enable Private Subnet).
One thing I hadn't thought of when submitting this was that my "skip" tags would be captured in the repo and exposed in my module tests; while they aren't secret or anything, it might look weird to external users. How do we feel about that? Would it be worth updating the workflows to pass the tags as part of the workflow rather than hard-coding them into the tests?

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
Hey @ericscheffler,
we had a conversation about this yesterday and fundamentally agreed to imeplement a solution - with the details still to be figured out.
The corner stones were roughly along the lines of
- Tags should be (optionally) injected by the CI into the test cases
- It should then be possible to pass these tags on into the shared templates (e.g., `dependencies.bicep`) where they would simply be added to all their resources (i.e., the template would have one `param tags object`, keeping the usage rather simple

What we still need to figure out is that injection part for which I want to set up a brainstorming session and collect some ideas to keep it as simple as possible to set up.

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
Hola @ericscheffler,
wie just had a quick brainstorming sessions and agreed to implement a PoC using the logic that we already have in place (i.e., you could already test it out today). The main points are
- We'd re-use the existing env-specific 'variable/secrets' injection logic ([ref](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/contributing/bicep/bicep-contribution-flow/custom-ci-secrets/))
- That means, after setting this logic up (which is a key vault + GH variable) one could
   1. Define a secret called e.g., `CI-CustomTags` with a value of `{ "tagA": "valueA", "tagB": "valueB" }`
   2. Define a parameter in the `main.test.bicep` test case like `param customTags string?`
   3. Pass its value to e.g., the `diagnostic.dependencies.bicep` as `tags: json(customTags)` (assuming the `tags` parameter was added to the dependency-template(s) before)
   4. And be in the happy zone

You could even pass the parameter into the `dependencies.bicep` or the main test, even if it has tags hardcoded. For the latter that would look like
```bicep
tags: union(
  {
    'hidden-title': 'This is visible in the resource name'
    Environment: 'Non-Prod'
    Role: 'DeploymentValidation'
  },
  json(tags)
)
``` 

I'll try to test this out in the near future, but cannot commit to a timeline yet with TechConnect upcoming etc. But you should be able to use this already today.

cc: @eriqua , @krbar

comments_list.author: segraef
comments_list.body:
Thanks @ArneRanvik, the schema supports this - `Microsoft.Consumption/budgets` notifications independently carry `operator` + `thresholdType` (`Actual`/`Forecasted`) per notification.

Going additive (non-breaking). Spec for the implementation:

1. In `avm/res/consumption/budget/sub-scope/main.bicep`, add a user-defined type:
   ```bicep
   @export()
   type notificationType = {
     operator: 'EqualTo' | 'GreaterThan' | 'GreaterThanOrEqualTo'
     @minValue(1) @maxValue(1000) threshold: int
     thresholdType: 'Actual' | 'Forecasted'
   }
   ```
2. Add `@maxLength(5) param notifications notificationType[]?` (optional).
3. When `notifications` is non-empty, build `notificationsArray` from it; otherwise fall back to the existing `thresholds` + `thresholdType` (preserves current behaviour - no breaking change).
4. Mark existing `thresholds` and `thresholdType` description with `Deprecated: use 'notifications' for per-threshold control.`
5. Mirror the change in `mg-scope/main.bicep` and `rg-scope/main.bicep`.
6. Update `README.md` (regen via `Set-AVMModule`), and add one test case using the new `notifications` param with mixed `Actual`/`Forecasted`.

Assigning Copilot.
