issues.author: oZakari
issues.body:
### Summary

`Get-DeploymentTargetResourceListInner` in `utilities/pipelines/e2eValidation/resourceRemoval/helper/Get-DeploymentTargetResourceList.ps1` cannot resolve nested deployments that target a different management group than the parent caller.

When recursing into a managementGroup-scoped child deployment, the function reuses the parent caller''s `$ManagementGroupId` instead of extracting the actual MG ID from the child deployment''s resource path (`/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<mgId>/...`). The subscription-path branch a few lines above does perform the equivalent extraction; the managementGroup branch was missing it.

### Impact

If the top-level test runs at `tenant` scope (no `-ManagementGroupId` set) and nests deployments into newly-created management groups (as is the case for `avm/ptn/mgmt-groups/subscription-placement`''s defaults test), the recursive call queries the operations API with an empty MG ID, the deployment is not found, and the catch-all path emits:

```
WARNING: Not found deployment [<name>] in scope [managementgroup]. Ignoring, as nested deployment.
```

Resources owned by those nested deployments (e.g. `Microsoft.Subscription/aliases`) are therefore never enumerated for removal. Cleanup later fails with `Cannot delete non-empty management group`, which is what surfaced on PR #6980.

### Why sub-vending''s own e2e didn''t hit this

- Sub-vending''s top-level template is `targetScope = ''managementGroup''`, so the runner is invoked with a real `-ManagementGroupId` and every nested deployment lives under that same MG. Reusing the parent value happens to be correct.
- The subscription alias resource is created at `tenant` scope and is resolved via the tenant branch, which has no MG ID to lose.

### Fix

Mirror the existing subscription-path behaviour and extract the MG ID from the deployment''s resource path before the recursive call.

### Closed by

Will be closed by #6980.

comments_list.author: htwashere
comments_list.body: Hello, we are experiencing a similar issue (same error message as this ticket). In our case, we have a generic bicep script using 'Microsoft.App/managedEnvironments@2024-10-02-preview'. The same script has been working fine for a long time. The interesting thing is that we had 3 team members ran the same script this week, only 1 faced this same error. This problem has only occurred for him starting this week. We compared our local environment, all have the same bicep version: Bicep CLI version 0.44.1 (28275db947). There is a mention above about dotNET, we were not changing anything dotNET related in ACE however, his local dotNET has been upgraded to 10 whereas the rest of us are on 8.0. Could the local bicep cli be using dotNET binaries behind the scene?

comments_list.author: htwashere
comments_list.body: Hello, just updating you again how we solved our similar problem above. After reporting on the last note, we changed our ACE bicep to the latest 'Microsoft.App/managedEnvironments@2026-01-01'. We also noticed that if we use the Azure Powershell library to invoke the bicep, we needed to update the az module: Update-Module -Name Az -Force. This has solved the problem for us. This is not to say it will solve the AVM script.

comments_list.author: nsftwr
comments_list.body:
For me this issue appeared when I tried to deploy two managed environments via `br/public:avm/res/app/managed-environment:0.13.3` within the same deployment. It complained with the same message. I diagnosed it that it only happens when two CAE's are deployed by commenting one and leaving the one thats failing, and reattempting the deployment. The one which was failing was now succeeding.

~I added a `dependsOn: [cae1]` to `cae2` deployment so the two cae's are deployed in sequence, and that resolved the issue.~

Edit: that fix made it from consistent failure to transient one where sometimes it will fail, sometimes not.

comments_list.author: memoryz
comments_list.body: I just ran into the same issue. Two consecutive deployments on the same resource, 1st one succeeded, 2nd one failed with this error.

issues.author: Mirabis
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/event-grid/system-topic

### (Optional) Module Version

 0.6.5

### Description

When `externalResourceRoleAssignments` targets a resource in a **different resource group** than the system topic, deployment fails with `ResourceNotFound`.

The generated inner role-assignment deployment (`*-EventGrid-SysTopic-ExtRoleAssign-*` → `*-ResourceRoleAssignment`) runs in the **system topic's** resource group and does not derive/set the target resource group from the supplied `resourceId`. ARM then resolves the extension-scope resource in the wrong RG.

### Repro

```bicep
// deployed into RG "rg-topic"; destination SA lives in "rg-dest"
module systemTopic 'br/public:avm/res/event-grid/system-topic:0.6.5' = {
  name: 'st'
  params: {
    name: 'st-demo'
    source: '<source SA resourceId in rg-topic>'
    topicType: 'Microsoft.Storage.StorageAccounts'
    managedIdentities: { systemAssigned: true }
    externalResourceRoleAssignments: [
      {
        resourceId: '/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/rg-dest/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/<destSa>'
        roleDefinitionId: 'c6a89b2d-59bc-44d0-9896-0f6e12d7b80a' // Storage Queue Data Message Sender
        roleName: 'Storage Queue Data Message Sender'
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Observed (deployment operation on inner `*-ResourceRoleAssignment`)

```
code:    ResourceNotFound
target:  .../resourceGroups/rg-dest/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/<destSa>/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/<guid>
message: "The Resource 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/<destSa>' under resource group 'rg-topic' was not found."
```

The role-assignment **id** correctly points at `rg-dest`, but ARM looks for the destination under `rg-topic` (the deployment's RG).

Note: `az deployment group validate` **and** `what-if` both report success — neither catches the cross-RG write rejection; it only surfaces at actual deploy.

### Expected

`externalResourceRoleAssignments` should support destinations in any RG/subscription by deriving `resourceGroup`/`subscriptionId` from the provided `resourceId` and setting them on the nested role-assignment deployment (as `avm/ptn/authorization/resource-role-assignment` already supports when called directly with an explicit `scope`).

### Workaround

Call `avm/ptn/authorization/resource-role-assignment` as a separate module with explicit `scope: resourceGroup(<destRg>)`, and set `externalResourceRoleAssignments: []`.

### (Optional) Correlation Id

69c25a0c-f98a-440a-b638-21d88c9df767

issues.author: kmosti
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/event-hub/namespace

### (Optional) Module Version

0.12.1 (also applies to 0.14.x)

### Description

Each event hub, consumer group, and per-hub authorization rule is deployed as its own module, and every module is a separate `Microsoft.Resources/deployments` record. With a lot of event hubs this fills up the 800 limit history fast.

I have a namespace with ~170 event hubs, two consumer groups each. One deployment of the namespace produces 500+ deployment records in the resource group. The RG is now sitting at 660 and a single run gets me close to the 800 limit, after which deployments start failing until grooming catches up.

0.12.4 ("eventhub as child module") and 0.14.2 ("Publish children") made this worse by splitting the children into separate modules.

Child resources declared inline don't create nested deployments, so this is purely a packaging choice that happens to be expensive at scale:

```
namespace
 └─ eventhub[i]          1 deployment each
     └─ consumergroup[j]  1 deployment each
     └─ authrule[k]       1 deployment each
```

### Suggested fix

Either declare `eventhubs` / `consumergroups` / per-hub `authorizationRules` as inline child resource loops instead of modules, or add a flag to opt into flat deployment for large namespaces. Both keep the count to a small constant regardless of event hub count.

### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

comments_list.author: kmosti
comments_list.body:
Just to add some context to why I think this is critical, given a scenario where:

1. The deployment history in a given resource group is empty
2. You have one consumer group in addition to the `$Default` per event hub
3. You have one auth rule per event hub

You would end up with:

### overhead
* deployment wrapper
* the `avm/res/event-hub/namespace` module itself
* `avmTelemetry` (optional)
* namespace authrule for the `RootManageSharedAccessKey`

### per event hub:
* the event hub module itself
* consumer groups: $Default + 1 additional
* auth rule

So: `4+(4N)` total, capping the maximum event hubs you could deploy with `avm/res/event-hub/namespace` at **199 event hubs** (although in practice this would be substantially fewer, depending on what else you may be deploying in your RG plus pre-existing deployment records).

comments_list.author: kmosti
comments_list.body: @elanzel @abhishekaryams do you need anything further from me at this point? I can propose a PR, but I would like to know if using a flag would be the desired direction to go or not.

comments_list.author: kmosti
comments_list.body: @jtracey93 is there a way to get some attention to this issue?

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
comments_list.body:
Hola @kmosti,
please excuse not getting around to this issue sooner as I was working through my GitHub notifications.
I'll reach out to other core team members to respond too.

My take is that this is unfortunate, yet by-design, so much so that you can find an AVM specification for it here: [BCPRMNFR3 - Child resources structure](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/spec/BCPRMNFR3/). Also, it's not EventHub-specific, but is true for all AVM (and former CARML) modules.
The jest of it is that we require child-modules to be implemented as they own deployment to be able to publish them independently and align them in structure with their namespace. As you already pointed out, this can clash with the [800 deployments limit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/troubleshooting/deployment-quota-exceeded?tabs=azure-cli) which is a limitation in Azure we have no control over. That makes it somewhat similar to the 4MB limit for templates which AVM also clashes with for very large pattern modules. 
In either case, the Product Group is looking to push these limits but have not shared any timelines with us yet.

You pointed out the alternative to opt-in/opt-out of the nesting which is a fair ask, but would require not only a duplication of much of AVM's code across all modules (as we try to keep modules as consistent as possible), to the detriment of testing & maintainability, but would make it much more likely to hit the 4MB limit mentioned above.

Personally, I can't see that we change this approach, but as said before will ask other maintainers to chime in too to share their thoughts.
To help your situation my next best (though painful) idea would be to slice and dice the deployment into groups of event hubs, each deployed by their own template - IF - some sort of grouping is possible. If run through a multi-runner setup, a parallel deployment should be possible, keeping the deployment time low. It's not a good solution, but it should work.

Related issue: https://github.com/Azure/bicep/issues/18621

comments_list.author: jtracey93
kmosti
comments_list.body:
Thanks @AlexanderSehr and @jtracey93 for picking this up, and no problem on the delay.

To be a bit blunt: as packaged today, `avm/res/event-hub/namespace` is not fit for our use case, and if the answer is "by design, no change", we will have to stop consuming it.

I understand why the spec is written the way it is, and I am not arguing that the AVM team is being unreasonable. I am arguing that the trade-off documented in `BCPRMNFR3` is not a pragmatic one from the consumer side once a namespace has more than a few dozen children.

> Kristian Mosti (@kmosti) do you care about the deployment history or do you never look at it once deployed?

We care about deployment failures, otherwise the deployment history is not used.

The problem is that the history is:

* a quota
* per resource group
* shared with everything else deployed into that resource group

AVM's child-module packaging spends that quota on our behalf, at a rate we do not control.

Two secondary effects that also matter to us:

- Automatic grooming is not a reliable mitigation, as you also note in Azure/bicep#18621.  
  Having consumers write a GC job to work around a module's packaging is a strong smell.
- Wall-clock deployment time. Every child is an ARM deployment with its own submit,
  validate and poll cycle, and ARM throttles the fan-out.


> That makes it somewhat similar to the 4MB limit for templates which AVM also clashes with for very large pattern modules.

Worth noting: this is not a "very large pattern module" edge case comparable to the 4MB limit. It is a single resource module deploying a single namespace.

> To help your situation my next best (though painful) idea would be to slice and dice the deployment into groups of event hubs, each deployed by their own template - IF - some sort of grouping is possible. If run through a multi-runner setup, a parallel deployment should be possible, keeping the deployment time low. It's not a good solution, but it should work.

I do not think slicing the event hubs into groups deployed by separate templates actually helps, and I would appreciate a correction if I have this wrong.
The 800 limit is per resource group. All the child deployments land in the same resource group regardless of how many top-level templates we split them into, so the total number of records is unchanged (slightly higher, because each shard adds its own wrapper).

Sharding only helps if the shards target different resource groups, which is impossible here because the event hubs must live in one namespace in one resource group. Running the shards serially with a grooming step in between could work, but that is a manual GC workaround which smells really bad (and would multiply our deployment time).

> ... but would make it (`opt-in/out`) much more likely to hit the 4MB limit mentioned above.

The size argument is fair. I would expect that delta to be modest relative to the nested-deployment scaffolding it sits next to, and I am happy to measure it on `event-hub/namespace` and post the before/after byte counts if that would make the decision easier.

### My (not-so-humble) ask

In decreasing order of ambition:

1. **An opt-in flag** on namespace-style modules with unbounded child fan-out, for example `flattenChildDeployments`.  
   This would not need to land across all AVM modules, only the handful where a parent can have an unbounded number of children: Event Hubs, Service Bus, Storage, SQL (AFAIK)
2. **Upstream fix in Bicep**, i.e. a way to consume a module without materialising a nested deployment. This is the sustainable answer and would let AVM keep BCPRMNFR3 exactly as written.
3. **If neither**: document the scale ceiling in the module README, e.g. "not suitable for more than roughly N `resource X` per resource group". This lets consumers make an informed choice up front instead of discovering it at 660 deployment records in production.


Happy to jump on a call if that is faster than a comment thread (:

comments_list.author: AlexanderSehr
matsest
comments_list.body:
Posted a similar ask in the Bicep repo: https://github.com/Azure/bicep/issues/20227

Even though this issue is most prevalent in AVM-modules - we've also had to refactor multiple AVM-modules to our own registry to avoid these errors - I think this should be looked at upstream from the Bicep side. Happy to give more input if needed, but I think @kmosti comment and suggestions give a good background and suggested solutions here.

### (Optional) Module Version

### Description

Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have searched existing issues for this module and found none matching this request.

Module Name

avm/res/cognitive-services/account

(Optional) Module Version

0.14.2, 0.15.0 (both inspected — gap present in both)

Description

GA Anthropic Claude models are ARM-deployable through Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments, but they require a modelProviderData attestation block (sibling of model) and api-version >= 2026-05-01. The current account module cannot pass this through, so consumers must drop to a raw-ARM nested-deployment lane.

Requesting first-class, backward-compatible support for modelProviderData.

confirm no default flips on accounts/deployments between versions.
- Consider @batchSize(1) on the deployment loop — the RP rejects concurrent deployment creates on a single account (observed during raw-ARM deploys). Can be split into a separate concurrency issue.

Interim raw-ARM lane (works today)

Until this lands, Anthropic models deploy via a nested raw-ARM template (untyped template object, so modelProviderData survives):

```bicep
@batchSize(1)
resource claudeModelDeployments 'Microsoft.Resources/deployments@2022-09-01' = [for d in deployments: {
  name: 'claude-model-${d.name}'
  properties: {
    mode: 'Incremental'
    template: {
      '$schema': 'https://schema.management.azure.com/schemas/2019-04-01/deploymentTemplate.json#'
      contentVersion: '1.0.0.0'
      resources: [
        {
          type: 'Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments'
          apiVersion: '2026-05-01'
          name: '${aiServicesName}/${d.name}'
          sku: { name: string(d.sku.name), capacity: int(d.sku.capacity) }
          properties: {
            model: { format: string(d.model.format), name: string(d.model.name), version: string(d.model.version) }
            modelProviderData: d.?modelProviderData ?? {}
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}]
```

Verification performed

- Deployed claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-8, claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5 (GlobalStandard) via az rest PUT with the body above; all reached provisioningState = Succeeded.
- Confirmed modelProviderData placement is properties.modelProviderData (sibling of model), api-version 2026-05-01.
- Confirmed AVM 0.14.2 / 0.15.0 compiled output omits the property and pins 2025-06-01.

N/A

issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/api-management/service

### (Optional) Module Version

0.14.4

### Description

When a service-scope policy (the `policies` param) or an API-scope policy (`apis[].policies`) references an APIM named value via a `{{token}}`, deployment intermittently fails because the policy module is applied in parallel with - and can win the race against - the `named-value` module. APIM validates `{{token}}` references at policy-apply time, so if the named value doesn't exist yet the RP returns:
```
ValidationError: Cannot find a property 'rl-global-limit'
Target: rate-limit-by-key
```

**Root cause**
In `main.bicep`,  module service_policies 'policy/main.bicep'  has no `dependsOn`:
```bicep
module service_policies 'policy/main.bicep' = [
  for (policy, index) in (policies ?? []): {
    name: '${uniqueString(deployment().name, location)}-Apim-Pol-${index}'  // -Apim-Policy-${index} in 0.12.0
    params: { apiManagementServiceName: service.name, value: policy.value, format: policy.?format, ... }
    // <-- missing: dependsOn: [ service_namedValues ]
  }
]
```
There is already a precedent in the same module - `service_loggers` correctly declares the dependency:
```bicep
module service_loggers 'logger/main.bicep' = [ for ... : {
  ...
  dependsOn: [ service_namedValues ]
} ]
```
**Expected behavior**
Any policy that can reference `{{named-value}}` tokens should be deployed after all named values.

**Proposed fix**

1. Add `dependsOn: [ service_namedValues ]` to `service_policies`.
2. Add `service_namedValues` to `service_apis`'s `dependsOn`.

**Repro**
Deploy the module with one named value and a service-scope policy that references it:
```bicep
namedValues: [ { name: 'rl-global-limit', displayName: 'rl-global-limit', value: '1000' } ]
policies:   [ { format: 'xml', value: '<policies><inbound><base /><rate-limit-by-key calls="{{rl-global-limit}}" renewal-period="60" counter-key="global" /></inbound>...</policies>' } ]
```

### (Optional) Correlation Id

e44b4f7f-56fd-4998-a9da-63aab8e083c1

it has been a while. Any chance you could triage this issue? Should be a very low hanging fruit :)

> Edit:

>
>https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/blob/affa2faab652283929d6cf8303d46816fe935bf8/avm/res/web/site/main.bicep#L77-L78

>Now, this were still the ARM days, we could just reference said API version as ARM is just a reversed engineered REST call. Unforatunately, Bicep is not that flexible and in order to expose said property via the new API version we'd need to inject ARM into Bicep. For this feature I'd advice against that and simply wait until likely the next Bicep version which usually also comes with new API versions.
> Once the version is available, the module would need to be upgraded (that is, both the resource & resource-derived type).

issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/cognitive-services/account

### (Optional) Module Version

0.15.0 and later, including the planned 0.16.0 from #7199

### Description


### Related PR

Follow-up to #7199 and its unresolved review comment:

> This should be implemented as a child resource.

### Description

In #7199, the `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments` resource was initially declared inline inside `account/main.bicep`.

To address the review feedback, the proposed implementation moves this child resource into a dedicated local child module:

`avm/res/cognitive-services/account/deployment/main.bicep`

The parent account module continues to expose the existing `deployments` parameter and delegates each deployment to the child module. This preserves the existing public module interface while separating the child-resource implementation.

The child module also contains the `modelProviderData` support introduced in #7199 for GA partner models such as Anthropic Claude.

### Proposed structure

```text
avm/res/cognitive-services/account/
├── main.bicep
├── deployment/
```

issues.body:
### Module Name

`avm/res/container-registry/registry`

### Module Version

`0.12.1`

### Issue Type

Security Bug

### Description

The `webhook` child module of `avm/res/container-registry/registry` declares `param customHeaders object?` without the `@secure()` decorator, while `serviceUri` is correctly marked `@secure()`. Webhook custom headers commonly carry authentication material (e.g. an `Authorization` header), so this parameter can flow a sensitive value without secure handling. Building the module raises the linter warning `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` on the webhook submodule, which also blocks consumers enforcing a 0-warning gate.

**Expected:** `customHeaders` marked `@secure()` (or a documented rationale), so the module builds without the warning.

**Actual (0.12.1 and current `main`):** `param customHeaders object?` is not secure → `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs`.

**Repro:**
```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules.git tmp
git -C tmp checkout -f avm/res/container-registry/registry/0.12.1
az bicep build --file tmp/avm/res/container-registry/registry/main.bicep
# → Warning use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs in webhook/main.bicep
```

Isolation note: reproduced with and without any custom linter config — the warning is intrinsic to the submodule source and not suppressible from a consumer's `bicepconfig.json`.
issues.title: [AVM Module Issue]: container-registry/registry webhook customHeaders should be @secure() (triggers use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs)

issues.body:
### Module Name

`avm/ptn/authorization/policy-assignment`

### Module Version

`0.5.3` (latest as of 2026-07-13; also reproducible on earlier versions — the ternary output pattern predates 0.5.3)

### Issue Type

Bug

### Description

`main.bicep` resolves its 4 outputs (`name`, `principalId`, `resourceId`, `location`) with a nested ternary that selects between 3 conditional submodules (`policyAssignment_mg`, `policyAssignment_sub`, `policyAssignment_rg` — one per scope, each declared conditionally so its type is `module | null`). The Bicep compiler cannot statically prove that exactly one of the 3 modules is deployed on each ternary branch, and emits `BCP318` ("The value of type 'module | null' may be null...") on every `.outputs.*` access — 12 occurrences in total (3 submodules × 4 outputs; lines 191, 193, 194, 198, 200, 201, 205, 207, 208, 212, 214, 215 in the 0.5.3 source).

**Expected:** building/linting a published AVM module yields 0 warnings for consumers enforcing a standard 0-warning gate. The exclusive-scope ternary pattern could be restructured so the compiler can prove non-nullability, or the diagnostic could be explicitly suppressed in-source with a rationale if it is considered an intentional false positive.

**Actual (0.5.3):** `az bicep build` / `az bicep lint` on `main.bicep` emits 12× `Warning BCP318` (EXIT 0 — non-blocking, but it breaks any consumer-side 0-warnings gate).

**Repro:**
```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules.git tmp
git -C tmp checkout -f avm/ptn/authorization/policy-assignment/0.5.3
az bicep build --file tmp/avm/ptn/authorization/policy-assignment/main.bicep
# → 12x Warning BCP318 in main.bicep(191,193,194,198,200,201,205,207,208,212,214,215)
```

Isolation note: reproduced with and without any custom linter config — `BCP318` is a core compiler diagnostic, not a linter rule suppressible via `bicepconfig.json`.

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

I'm not sure

### Module Name

avm/res/api-management/service

### (Optional) Module Version

0.14.4

### Description

## Description

While using the `avm/res/api-management/service/identity-provider` module, I noticed an inconsistency between the `name` and `type` parameters.

The module currently restricts `type` to a specific set of allowed identity providers, but `name` is defined as a free-form string. However, according to the underlying ARM/Bicep resource definition, the resource name itself must match one of the supported identity provider names (for example `aad`, `facebook`, `google`, `microsoft`, `twitter`, etc.).

As a result, both `name` and `type` effectively represent the same provider identifier and must be selected from the same fixed list.

## Current Behavior

```bicep
module identityProvider 'br/public:avm/res/api-management/service/identity-provider:<version>' = {
  name: 'identityProvider'
  params: {
    name: 'my-custom-name' // Appears valid from AVM typing
    type: 'google'
    ...
  }
}
```

The module allows any string for `name`, but the deployment will only succeed when the resource name corresponds to a supported identity provider.

## Expected Behavior

The `name` parameter should either:

1. Use the same allowed values as `type`, or
2. Be derived automatically from `type`, removing the possibility of supplying inconsistent values.

Example:

```bicep
@allowed([
  'aad'
  'facebook'
  'google'
  'microsoft'
  'twitter'
])
param name string
```

or

```bicep
param type string

resource identityProvider ... = {
  name: type
  ...
}
```

## Why This Matters

Currently the module allows invalid configurations that are only caught during deployment rather than at Bicep validation time.

Aligning the validation of `name` with `type` would:

- Improve type safety
- Prevent invalid deployments
- Better reflect the underlying APIM resource requirements
- Provide a more consistent AVM authoring experience

## References

- AVM module: https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/tree/main/avm/res/api-management/service/identity-provider
- Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/identityProviders documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.apimanagement/service/identityproviders?pivots=deployment-language-bicep

## Suggested Approach

I would personally lean toward removing `name` as an independent parameter and deriving it from `type`, since APIM identity providers are effectively singleton resources identified by the provider type itself. That would eliminate the possibility of supplying conflicting values altogether.

---
Note: English is not my first language, and I am dyslexic. I used AI assistance to help draft and improve the wording of this issue. The technical observations and findings are my own.

issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have searched for previous/existing GitHub issues.

### Module Name

`avm/res/network/virtual-hub`

### (Optional) Module Version

`0.4.3`

### Description

The module sets two optional, nullable routing-preference properties **unconditionally** on the `Microsoft.Network/virtualHubs` resource:

```bicep
hubRoutingPreference: hubRoutingPreference
preferredRoutingGateway: preferredRoutingGateway
```

Both parameters are declared optional and nullable. When either is left unset, Bicep does not omit the property — it compiles to a present key with a null value in the resource body (`"hubRoutingPreference": null` / `"preferredRoutingGateway": null`). A present routing-preference property (including a null, or the value `'None'` for `preferredRoutingGateway`) is rejected by ARM with:

```
Code: VirtualWanRoutingPreferenceFeatureTypeNotSupported
Virtual Wan Routing Preference type is not supported.
```

and the hub is never created. This blocks any deployment that does not explicitly want a routing preference, even on subscriptions where the routing-preference feature is registered.

### Root cause

The properties should be included in the resource body only when a value is supplied. A **genuinely absent** key lets ARM apply its own default and provisions cleanly. Confirmed by isolation testing directly against the API (no module):

- A bare `virtualHubs` resource with **both** keys absent provisions to `Succeeded`; ARM applies its default routing preference.
- The same resource with `hubRoutingPreference` present as null **fails** with the error above.
- The same resource differing only by `preferredRoutingGateway: 'None'` **fails** with the identical error.

So it is the *presence* of the property that trips the feature gate, not its value, and the two properties are the same defect in sibling fields.

### Affected versions

Confirmed in `0.4.3`. The same unconditional assignment appears in later versions of the module, which are expected to be affected identically.

### Suggested fix

Include each property only when non-null, so an unset optional property is omitted from the request body, e.g.:

```bicep
...(hubRoutingPreference != null ? { hubRoutingPreference: hubRoutingPreference } : {})
...(preferredRoutingGateway != null ? { preferredRoutingGateway: preferredRoutingGateway } : {})
```

### Expected behaviour

Leaving `hubRoutingPreference` and/or `preferredRoutingGateway` unset should omit them from the resource body and let ARM apply its defaults, rather than emitting a present key and failing with `VirtualWanRoutingPreferenceFeatureTypeNotSupported`.

comments_list.author: myaschmitz
comments_list.body:
Thanks for the detailed writeup — the code observation is right, but I can't reproduce the failure through the module, and I don't think the suggested fix would change the emitted request.

ARM strips null-valued properties during template evaluation, before the request reaches the Network RP ([docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/template-expressions#null-values): "Resource Manager templates treat it as if the property isn't present"). So with both parameters unset, the module already sends a body with neither key — the same body the suggested spread would produce.

Verified two ways:

- `what-if` against `main.json` with only `name`, `addressPrefix`, and `virtualWanResourceId` set: the proposed hub properties are `addressPrefix`, `allowBranchToBranchTraffic`, `sku`, and `virtualWan`. Neither routing property is present.
- The module's `defaults` e2e test passes exactly those three parameters and deploys successfully: [run 30957985640](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/30957985640).

I suspect the isolation test is where this diverges — a direct API call has no template evaluation step, so a literal `"hubRoutingPreference": null` in a hand-written body does reach the RP and is rejected. Accurate reproduction, but of a path the module doesn't take.

The `preferredRoutingGateway: 'None'` case is real and separate: `'None'` is a non-null value, so it is sent and the RP rejects it. The module derives that enum from the API schema via `resourceInput<...>`, so a value being advertised but unsupported is upstream of AVM.

Closing as not reproducible. If you're hitting this on a real template deployment, please reopen with the deployment's correlation ID and the parameters passed — that would point at a different cause.

issues.title: avm/res/network/virtual-hub: hubRoutingPreference and preferredRoutingGateway emitted unconditionally, blocking hub creation when unset

### Description

I wanted to make you aware of an issue that is currently preventing deployment validation from completing successfully for part of our Azure infrastructure.

The deployment relies on an Azure Verified Module (AVM) for managing Azure resources. AVMs are Microsoft-supported Infrastructure-as-Code modules that provide a standard way to deploy and manage Azure services. Internally, these modules use specific Azure Resource Manager (ARM) API versions when communicating with Azure.

In this case, the AVM module currently being used is referencing an older API version for the affected resources. However, the existing resources have been configured with functionality that is only supported through a newer API version. During validation, Azure detects this mismatch and rejects the deployment because the older API version cannot manage resources that contain the newer functionality.

As a result, deployment validation fails even though the deployment configuration itself appears to be correct.

Could you please engage the team responsible for maintaining the infrastructure modules/platform components to review this dependency and determine the appropriate path forward? This will likely require either:

Updating the AVM module to a version that supports the newer Azure API version; or
Modifying the deployment solution to use a newer API version that is compatible with the current resource configuration.

Until the module/API version alignment is addressed, deployments affecting these resources are likely to continue failing validation.

Please let me know if you need any additional technical details or the full validation error output.

Thanks

issues.author: StefNikolaou
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/db-for-postgre-sql/flexible-server

### (Optional) Module Version

0.16.0

### Description

The configuration child module in PostgreSQL Flexible Server AVM module
version `0.16.0` uses the following preview API:

```bicep
Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/configurations@2026-01-01-preview
```

We observed that some static PostgreSQL configurations reported a
successful deployment but were not persisted on the server.

The affected settings included:

- `shared_preload_libraries`
- `shared_buffers`

For example:

```bicep
module flexibleServer 'br/public:avm/res/db-for-postgre-sql/flexible-server:0.16.0' = {
  params: {
    // Other required server parameters omitted for brevity.
    configurations: [
      {
        name: 'shared_buffers'
        value: '1500000'
        source: 'user-override'
      }
      {
        name: 'shared_preload_libraries'
        value: 'pg_cron,pg_stat_statements'
        source: 'user-override'
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The deployment and the individual configuration resources reported
`Succeeded`. However, querying the server afterwards showed that the
previous values remained:

- `shared_buffers` remained `786432`
- `shared_preload_libraries` remained `timescaledb`

A dynamic setting such as `azure.extensions` was applied successfully,
while the static settings above remained unchanged.

We understand that `2026-01-01-preview` is a preview API and its behavior
may change. The concern is that the AVM module hardcodes this API for
configuration resources, while the stable `2024-08-01` API supports the
same child-resource type. Module consumers cannot select the stable API.

As a workaround, we deployed the configurations through a small module
using the stable API:

```bicep
targetScope = 'resourceGroup'

@description('Name of the PostgreSQL flexible server.')
param flexibleServerName string

@description('Name of the PostgreSQL server configuration.')
param name string

@description('Source of the PostgreSQL server configuration.')
param source string?

@description('Value of the PostgreSQL server configuration.')
param value string?

resource flexibleServer 'Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers@2024-08-01' existing = {
  name: flexibleServerName
}

resource configuration 'Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/configurations@2024-08-01' = {
  name: name
  parent: flexibleServer
  properties: {
    source: source
    value: value
  }
}
```

The configurations were deployed serially using `@batchSize(1)`. With
the stable `2024-08-01` API, the requested static values were persisted
successfully.

#### Expected behavior

When a configuration resource reports `Succeeded`, its configured value
should reflect the requested value.

For settings requiring a restart, the setting may be marked as pending
restart, but the configuration resource should still contain the newly
requested value.

#### Actual behavior

The configuration deployment reports `Succeeded`, but the static
configuration value remains unchanged.

#### Request

Could the PostgreSQL configuration child module use the stable
`2024-08-01` API?

If the preview API is required, could the team clarify the reason and
investigate or document the observed behavior for static PostgreSQL
settings?

It would also be helpful to include an integration test that deploys a
static setting and verifies its value after deployment.

We cannot conclusively determine whether the underlying cause belongs to
the AVM module or the PostgreSQL resource provider. The stable API
workaround indicates that the behavior is related to the API version.


### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

comments_list.author: StefNikolaou
comments_list.body:
Some additional reproduction details:

- The affected resource was an existing PostgreSQL Flexible Server running PostgreSQL 16 in euw.
- The server was in the `Ready` state when the configurations were deployed.
- AVM `0.16.0` already deploys configuration modules serially using
  `@batchSize(1)`, so serialization was present in both the failing AVM
  deployment and the successful workaround.
- The values were checked through the Azure configuration resource after
  deployment, for example:

  ```powershell
  az postgres flexible-server parameter show `
    --resource-group <resource-group> `
    --server-name <server-name> `
    --name shared_preload_libraries
  ```

- This was not only a case of PostgreSQL requiring a restart before using
  the new value. The Azure configuration resource itself continued to
  return the previous value after the deployment had reported `Succeeded`.
- Deploying the same requested value with
  `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/configurations@2024-08-01`
  updated the configuration resource successfully.

issues.author: sebastiaanvandesteeg
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/api-management/service

### (Optional) Module Version

0.14.4

### Description

The module declares:

```bicep
@description('Conditional. The scale units for this API Management service. Required if using Basic, Standard, or Premium skus. For range of capacities for each sku, reference https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/api-management/.')
param skuCapacity int = 3
```

`skuCapacity` defaults to `3` regardless of the chosen `sku`. This default is invalid for the `Basic` tier, which only supports a capacity of `1` or `2`. When a consumer sets `sku: 'Basic'` without explicitly overriding `skuCapacity`, deployment fails with:

```
OutOfBoundSkuCapacityForSkuType: Specified Sku capacity of 3 is invalid. For Basic Sku it must be between 1 and 2, inclusive. Add CustomSettings if needed.
```

This is surprising because the module's `Developer` handling already accounts for tier-specific constraints (capacity is hardcoded to `1` for `Developer` in the `service` resource: `contains(sku, 'Developer') ? 1 : skuCapacity`), but no equivalent safeguard/default exists for `Basic`.

# Repro

```bicep
module apiManagement 'br/public:avm/res/api-management/service:0.14.4' = {
  params: {
    name: 'apim-example'
    location: location
    publisherEmail: 'api@example.com'
    publisherName: 'Example'
    sku: 'Basic'
    // skuCapacity omitted, defaults to 3 -> deployment fails
  }
}
```

# Expected behavior / suggested fixes

- Lower the default `skuCapacity` to a value valid across all SKU tiers (e.g. `1` or `2`), since `1` is valid for every tier including `Basic` and `Developer`.
- Alternatively, add tier-aware capacity clamping/fallback logic in the `service` resource (similar to the existing `Developer` special-case), e.g. defaulting to `2` when `sku == 'Basic'` and `skuCapacity` is left unset/exceeds the tier's max.
- At minimum, document this pitfall more prominently in the parameter description, since the "Conditional... Required if using Basic, Standard, or Premium" wording doesn't make clear that the *default itself* is invalid for `Basic`.

# Workaround

Explicitly pass `skuCapacity: 1` (or `2`) when using `sku: 'Basic'`.


### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

issues.author: prutsert
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/recovery-services/vault

### (Optional) Module Version

_No response_

### Description

Module `avm/res/recovery-services/vault` has two different options to configure Soft Delete:
- Parameter `softDeleteSettings`, which is defined as: 
  ```
  type softDeleteSettingType = {
      enhancedSecurityState: ('AlwaysON' | 'Disabled' | 'Enabled' | 'Invalid')
      softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays: int
      softDeleteState: ('AlwaysON' | 'Disabled' | 'Enabled' | 'Invalid')
  }
  ```
- Parameter `backupConfig`, whose properties are used to create child resource `avm/res/recovery-services/vault/backup-config`, and (among others) has the properties:
  ```
  enhancedSecurityState
  softDeleteFeatureState
  isSoftDeleteFeatureStateEditable
  softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays
  ```

If both parameters exist, the first two properties of the `backupConfig` parameter will not be set, effectively falling back to the equivalent properties from `softDeleteSettings`:
```
enhancedSecurityState: !empty(softDeleteSettings) ? null : backupConfig.?enhancedSecurityState
softDeleteFeatureState: !empty(softDeleteSettings) ? null : backupConfig.?softDeleteFeatureState
```
The latter two do not follow that behaviour, and will get set:
```
isSoftDeleteFeatureStateEditable: backupConfig.?isSoftDeleteFeatureStateEditable
softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays: backupConfig.?softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays
```

A few observations:
1. The `softDeleteSettings` parameter properties `enhancedSecurityState` and `softDeleteState` will overrule the corresponding properties in the `backupConfig` parameter, when both are passed as input to a deployment.
1. Both parameters contain a third shared property, `softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays`, which can be abiguously passed with different values, and will not be overruled.
1. The `backupConfig` parameter has a property `isSoftDeleteFeatureStateEditable`, which appears to be relevant to the Soft Delete feature, but can't be configured using the `softDeleteSettings` parameter. According to the bicep/ARM documentation: "_This flag is no longer in use. Please use 'softDeleteFeatureState' to set the soft delete state for the vault_".

A few questions:
1. Which value for `softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays` is leading, and shouldn't the override mechanism be implemented for this parameter as well?
1. Is the usage of a specific one of the parameters preferable over the other, for example because the other may be deprecated in the future?
1. Since we would like to use only one of these parameters whenever possible, do the other properties of `backupConfig`, such as `storageModelType`, `storageType` and `storageTypeState`, also map to `recovery-services/vault` parameters, so we can be sure to configure them only once?


### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

comments_list.author: alexanderojala
comments_list.body:
Thanks for the detailed write-up @prutsert 

The core bug is that `softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays `in `backupConfig `isn't being nulled out when `softDeleteSettings `is provided, unlike `enhancedSecurityState `and `softDeleteFeatureState `which already have that override logic. This can lead to ambiguous/conflicting values between the vault-level and backup-config resources.

I'm looking into a fix to apply the same override pattern to `softDeleteRetentionPeriodInDays `as well.

Regarding `isSoftDeleteFeatureStateEditable `— as you noted, Azure docs confirm this flag is deprecated, so it shouldn't need to be part of `softDeleteSettings`.

avm/res/key-vault/vault:0.14.0

still uses an older Key Vault control-plane API version, for example:

Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults@2024-11-01

Microsoft guidance recommends moving deployments to API version 2026-02-01 or later before the retirement date.

Reference:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/access-control-default

Could you please confirm whether there is a planned AVM release to update avm/res/key-vault/vault to:

Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults@2026-02-01

or a later supported stable API version?

This is particularly important for customers standardizing their Infrastructure-as-Code implementations on Azure Verified Modules. When consuming the published AVM module, customers cannot independently change the underlying Key Vault ARM API version without replacing or forking the AVM implementation.

Ideally, the AVM module should be updated sufficiently ahead of the underlying Resource Provider API retirement date so customers have enough time to upgrade, test, and deploy the newer AVM version across their environments.

It would also be helpful to clarify whether AVM modules are expected to be proactively updated when underlying Azure Resource Provider API versions are announced for retirement.

Expected outcome

A new release of avm/res/key-vault/vault that uses:

Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults@2026-02-01

or a later supported stable API version before the retirement of the older Key Vault control-plane APIs

We've just activated automatic checks for the [changelog spec BCPNFR22](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/spec/BCPNFR22/). Please update your branch and add an entry to the CHANGELOG.md.

Sample entry for the `CHANGELOG.md` in the module directory is:

```text
## 0.2.1

### Changes

- Updated the referenced AVM common types

### Breaking Changes

- None
```

> The new version is calculated automatically, and you must set the new version in the changelog manually. The static tests will show you the expected version if you set it to something else.

[SNFR17 - Category: Release - Semantic Versioning](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/spec/SNFR17/)

With a new minor version in the `version.json`, add **0** as patch. If you didn't change the version, the patch will be **patch+1**.

We are happy to help should you encounter a problem.

prs.body:
Adds support for configuring service endpoints on subnets within the sub-vending module. This change enables the definition and deployment of service endpoints, enhancing network security and connectivity options for resources within the subnet.

Fixes #6483

## Description
added line 
``` bicep
 serviceEndpoints: subnet.?serviceEndpoints
```

``` bicep
 subnets: [
      for (subnet, i) in virtualNetworkSubnets: (!empty(virtualNetworkSubnets))
        ? {
            name: subnet.name
            addressPrefix: subnet.?addressPrefix
            ipamPoolPrefixAllocations: subnet.?ipamPoolPrefixAllocations
            networkSecurityGroupResourceId: (virtualNetworkDeployBastion || subnet.name == 'AzureBastionSubnet')
              ? createBastionNsg.?outputs.resourceId
              : resourceId(
                  subscriptionId,
                  virtualNetworkResourceGroupName,
                  'Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups',
                  '${createLzNsg[i].?outputs.name}'
                )
            routeTableResourceId: (!empty(subnet.?routeTableName) && !empty(routeTablesResourceGroupName))
              ? resourceId(
                  subscriptionId,
                  routeTablesResourceGroupName,
                  'Microsoft.Network/routeTables',
                  subnet.?routeTableName ?? ''
                )
              : null
            natGatewayResourceId: virtualNetworkDeployNatGateway && (subnet.?associateWithNatGateway ?? false)
              ? createNatGateway.?outputs.resourceId
              : null
            delegation: subnet.?delegation
            serviceEndpoints: subnet.?serviceEndpoints
          }
        : {}
    ]
```

prs.author: Copilot
prs.body:
## Description

Storage account keys were exposed in ARM deployment templates when using the web/site config module with default settings, triggering Defender for Cloud alerts.

### Changes

- **Breaking**: Changed `storageAccountUseIdentityAuthentication` default from `false` to `true` in:
  - `avm/res/web/site/config/main.bicep`
  - `avm/res/web/site/slot/config/main.bicep`
- Enhanced parameter description to document security implications of `false` value

### Behavior Change

**Before:**
```bicep
configs: [{
  name: 'appsettings'
  storageAccountResourceId: sa.id
  // implicitly: storageAccountUseIdentityAuthentication = false
  // Result: storage keys exposed in deployment template
}]
```

**After:**
```bicep
configs: [{
  name: 'appsettings'
  storageAccountResourceId: sa.id
  // implicitly: storageAccountUseIdentityAuthentication = true
  // Result: identity-based auth, no key exposure
}]
```

Users requiring key-based auth must explicitly set `storageAccountUseIdentityAuthentication: false`.

### Requirements for Identity-Based Auth
- App Service managed identity configured
- `Storage Blob Data Owner` role assigned to storage account

prs.author: FallenHoot
prs.body:
## Description

This PR adds the **FinOps Hub** pattern module to Azure Verified Modules (AVM). FinOps Hub is a comprehensive cost management and optimization solution that ingests, normalizes, and analyzes cloud cost data from multiple providers.

## CI Status (Fork)
[![avm.ptn.finops-toolkit.finops-hub](https://github.com/FallenHoot/bicep-registry-modules/actions/workflows/avm.ptn.finops-toolkit.finops-hub.yml/badge.svg?branch=feature/finops-hub-avm-module)](https://github.com/FallenHoot/bicep-registry-modules/actions/workflows/avm.ptn.finops-toolkit.finops-hub.yml)

## Features

- **Multi-cloud support**: Ingest FOCUS-compliant cost data from Azure, AWS, GCP, and OCI
- **Flexible analytics backend**: Choose between Azure Data Explorer (ADX) or Microsoft Fabric
- **Pre-built analytics**: KQL functions for cost analysis, optimization recommendations, and reporting
- **Security options**: Optional managed virtual network for enhanced data protection
- **WAF-aligned**: Deployment options that follow Azure Well-Architected Framework best practices
- **EXPERIMENTAL dashboard**: ADX dashboard JSON with 19 pages covering cost analysis, commitments, optimization, and multi-cloud views

## Module Details

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Module Path | `avm/ptn/finops-toolkit/finops-hub` |
| Version | 1.0.0 |
| Type | Pattern (ptn) |
| Telemetry | `46d3xbcp.ptn.finopstoolkit-finopshub` |

## AVM Compliance

- ✅ Implements `lock` and `diagnosticSettings` standard interfaces
- ✅ Uses AVM common types from `avm/utl/types/avm-common-types:0.6.1`
- ✅ Follows AVM naming conventions and module structure
- ✅ Includes comprehensive e2e tests for all deployment scenarios (7 tests)
- ✅ Telemetry enabled via `enableTelemetry` parameter
- ✅ PSRule WAF alignment checks passing

## Test Scenarios

All 7 e2e test scenarios are **enabled and passing**:

| Test | Description | Status |
|------|-------------|--------|
| storage-minimal | Basic deployment with storage-only defaults | ✅ |
| adx-minimal | Minimal ADX deployment | ✅ |
| adx-waf-aligned | WAF-aligned ADX with managed identities, diagnostics | ✅ |
| adx-managed-network | ADX with managed virtual network | ✅ |
| fabric-minimal | Minimal Fabric deployment | ✅ |
| fabric-waf-aligned | WAF-aligned Fabric deployment | ✅ |
| managed-network | Managed virtual network configuration | ✅ |

## ADX Managed Identity Policy — Implementation Note

The ADX cluster requires a `managed_identity` policy for native ingestion via Azure Data Factory. We explored several approaches to automate this:

1. **Deployment Script with `scriptLevel: 'Cluster'`** — Works in CI but the database script resource has limitations with cluster-level KQL commands in some edge cases.
2. **Cluster Principal Assignment** — Grants broad admin roles; not granular enough for just ingestion policy.
3. **Direct REST API via deployment scripts** — Requires bearer token management and adds deployment complexity.

**Current approach**: The ADX managed identity policy is set via an **ADF pipeline activity** (`Set Ingestion Policy`) that runs as part of the `ingestion_ETL_dataExplorer` pipeline. This mirrors the [upstream FinOps Toolkit](https://github.com/microsoft/finops-toolkit) pattern where ADF manages ADX configuration as part of the data pipeline, rather than during ARM deployment.

We've engaged the ADX Product Group for guidance on a cleaner Bicep-native approach (e.g., a dedicated ARM resource type for MI policy). In the meantime, the ADF-based approach is reliable and production-tested.

## Related

- [FinOps Toolkit](https://github.com/microsoft/finops-toolkit)
- [FOCUS Specification](https://focus.finops.org/)
- [AVM Pattern Modules](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/specs/ptn/)

## Checklist

- [x] Module follows AVM specifications
- [x] All required interfaces implemented
- [x] Documentation complete (README.md)
- [x] E2E tests included and passing (all 7 scenarios)
- [x] Bicep compiles without errors
- [x] PSRule WAF alignment checks passing
- [x] main.json regenerated and CR-free
- [x] README.md regenerated via Set-ModuleReadMe

review_comments.body: Pushing back on this one. The upstream FinOps toolkit uses `scripts/` as the folder name, and since customers clone and reference this module directly, we want to keep alignment with the upstream project for consistency. review_comments.author: FallenHoot
review_comments.body:
This module is retained as a **legacy reference only** and is **not wired into the deployment graph**. Per ADR-013, ADX does not natively support executing cluster-level management commands (e.g., `.alter-merge cluster policy managed_identity`) through ARM-deployable resources — `Microsoft.Kusto/clusters/databases/scripts` is limited to database-scoped commands, and deployment scripts face a known ARM→ADX control-plane timing gap where principal assignments have not yet propagated. This limitation has been reported to the ADX Product Group.

The accepted workaround is to set the managed identity policy at runtime via an ADF `AzureDataExplorerCommand` pipeline activity (the 'Set Ingestion Policy' step in `dataFactoryResources.bicep`). We keep this file in case the ADX PG addresses the platform limitation in a future API version. Since it's unused, extracting the inline script to an external file isn't needed at this time.

## Description

The `kind` parameter value passed to the web app module is being replaced with a hardcoded `'app,linux'` value when any kind is specified. This breaks Windows App Service deployments because the staging slot gets created as Linux while the production site is Windows.

Found during deployment testing - the conditional on line 190 in `app-service.module.bicep`:

kind: !empty(kind) ? 'app,linux' : 'app'

This always evaluates to `'app,linux'` when a kind parameter is passed (e.g., `'app'` for Windows), regardless of what the actual value is. Changed to pass through the parameter value directly:

kind: kind

Error message encountered:

The slot 'kind' property 'app,linux' must match the Production site 'kind' property 'app'.

review_comments.author: eriqua
review_comments.body:
My main concern with this is that this would potentially result in a huge PR, which I personally don't support.

I believe it would be wiser to cover smaller scopes, for the time being, but optimizing it. Let's consider the API version check as an example. Updating the api version is not always as easy as changing the version. It involves new features, additional parameters, potentially, although not too often, even breaking changes. Not to mention new child resources. Depending on this, we should mention what version update we expect, major (not now), minor or patch. This is where we should leverage AI support imho. It's very much a skill on its own.

Once we have a few of those well scoped skills, we can think about implementing a "super skill".

I'd probably deprioritize content already fully covered by static validation. For example I'd avoid checking if we have waf-aligned and defaults tests. If we didn't, the module wouldn't be there. Note: the max test is not mandatory, so it's not correct to include it. Plus, "Deploys with all (or most) parameters set" is not providing clear guidance. Instead, what about: for a max test I would like to verify if all possible parameters are included and out of all possible parameters have a clear understanding of which parameters cannot be used together, as they would otherwise result in a conflict. Just food for thoughts

prs.author: danieletten
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #5561

Adds Confidential VM (CVM) support to the `avm/res/compute/virtual-machine` and `avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set` modules.

### Defect 1: uefiSettings is null when securityType == ConfidentialVM

The `uefiSettings` condition only matched `TrustedLaunch`. When `securityType` is `ConfidentialVM`, `uefiSettings` evaluated to null. Azure requires `secureBootEnabled: true` and `vTpmEnabled: true` for Confidential VMs.

**Fix:** Changed the condition to include both security types.

### Defect 2: OS disk managedDisk.securityProfile.securityEncryptionType is missing (VM module only)

There was no `securityProfile` object on the managed disk. Azure requires `osDisk.managedDisk.securityProfile.securityEncryptionType` to be set for Confidential VMs.

**Fix:** Added optional `securityProfile` (with `securityEncryptionType` and `diskEncryptionSetResourceId`) to the `osDiskType` and wired it into the VM resource.

> Note: The VMSS module uses `resourceInput<>` for osDisk, which inherits the schema from the ARM API and already includes securityProfile. No change needed there.

### Defect 3: Misleading parameter descriptions

The descriptions for `secureBootEnabled` and `vTpmEnabled` only mentioned TrustedLaunch.

**Fix:** Updated descriptions to mention both TrustedLaunch and ConfidentialVM.

### E2E Test

Added `windows.confidentialvm` E2E test validating:

- `securityType: 'ConfidentialVM'`
- `uefiSettings` (secureBootEnabled + vTpmEnabled)
- `osDisk.managedDisk.securityProfile.securityEncryptionType: 'VMGuestStateOnly'`
- VM size: `Standard_DC2as_v5` (DCasv5-series)

@sebassem what are your thoughts on this? Happy to also get on a call if need be to explain the thought, but essentially the idea is that a UMI can be provisioned together with the vended sub, but have the role assigned in a different sub or management group like connectivity sub, having the Private DNS Zone Contributor role.

The current implementation adds an `absoluteScope` property next to `relativeScope`. Ive done that so its not classified as a breaking change, but I am also happy to make it so property changes `relativeScope -> scope`, and have the functionality as 

- If `scope: ''` then role assignment is on the vended subscription
- if `scope: '/resourceGroups/rg-aabbcc` then role assignment is on the vended sub, scoped to the rg
- if `scope: '/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'` then the role assignment is on another sub
- if `scope: '/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-aabbcc'` then the role assignment is on the resource group in another sub
- if `scope: '/managementGroups/mg_corp'` then the role assignment is on the management group

Let me know what are your thoughts.

prs.author: oZakari
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #6900
Fixes #7125

The `customSubscriptionPlacement` module loop in `avm/ptn/mgmt-groups/subscription-placement` had an inverted condition. Subscriptions were only placed when `disableSubscriptionPlacement` was set to `true` — the opposite of the intended behaviour.

This change negates the condition (and uses `?? false` to safely handle the omitted/null case) so that:

- `disableSubscriptionPlacement` omitted → placement runs
- `disableSubscriptionPlacement: false` → placement runs
- `disableSubscriptionPlacement: true` → placement skipped

### Additional fix: e2e resource-removal helper (#7125)

While validating the fix, the e2e cleanup phase failed with `Cannot delete non-empty management group [test-mgmt-group]`. Root cause: `Get-DeploymentTargetResourceListInner` in `utilities/pipelines/e2eValidation/resourceRemoval/helper/Get-DeploymentTargetResourceList.ps1` reused the parent caller's `$ManagementGroupId` when recursing into managementGroup-scoped child deployments, instead of extracting the MG ID from the child deployment's resource path. The defaults test runs at tenant scope and nests deployments into newly-created MGs, so the recursive lookup queried the API with an empty MG ID and silently dropped the nested deployments (`Not found deployment ... Ignoring, as nested deployment.`). As a result `Microsoft.Subscription/aliases` was never enumerated for removal and the MG could not be deleted. The fix mirrors the existing subscription-path branch and extracts the actual MG ID from the deployment's resource path. See #7125 for full details.

prs.body:
## Description

The NetApp account module did not expose the Active Directory `site` field, which blocked parity with existing portal-configured AD integrations during migration to Bicep. This change adds an explicit module input and maps it to the ARM `activeDirectories[].site` property.

- **Module behavior**
  - Added new optional nullable parameter: `activeDirectorySite`.
  - Wired `activeDirectorySite` into `Microsoft.NetApp/netAppAccounts.properties.activeDirectories[].site`.
  - Emits `site` only when both `domainName` and `activeDirectorySite` are non-empty (avoids sending empty string values).

- **Generated artifacts**
  - Updated `main.json` to include the new parameter and compiled mapping.
  - Updated `README.md` to document `activeDirectorySite`, keep parameter ordering consistent, and clarify the site description.
  - Updated `CHANGELOG.md` with a new entry (`0.12.5`) for this enhancement.

```bicep
@description('Optional. The Active Directory site (as configured in Active Directory Sites and Services) the service will limit Domain Controller discovery to.')
param activeDirectorySite string?

var activeDirectoryConnectionProperties = [
  {
    // ...
    site: !empty(domainName) && !empty(activeDirectorySite) ? activeDirectorySite : null
  }
]
```

- **Test infrastructure**
  - Replaced the CMK test's sleep-only Azure deploymentScript with OIDC-authenticated runner-side dependency preparation and the same 15-second propagation wait.
  - Retained the actual CMK account deployment and cleanup tracking for both phases; no production-module changes were needed for this test fix and no Azure security controls were relaxed.

prs.author: Copilot
prs.body:
This change adds additive, per-notification control for budget alerts so a single budget can mix `Actual` and `Forecasted` notifications with independent operators. Existing behavior is preserved by keeping the current `thresholds` + `thresholdType` path as fallback when `notifications` is not provided.

- **Module contract changes (all scopes: sub/mg/rg)**
  - Added exported `notificationType` user-defined type with `operator`, bounded `threshold`, and `thresholdType`.
  - Added optional `@maxLength(5) param notifications notificationType[]?`.
  - Marked `thresholds` and `thresholdType` descriptions as deprecated in favor of `notifications`.

- **Notification composition logic**
  - When `notifications` is non-empty, resource notifications are built from it.
  - Otherwise, notifications are derived from legacy `thresholds` + `operator` + `thresholdType` to keep compatibility.

- **Generated module artifacts**
  - Regenerated scoped `README.md` and `main.json` files for `sub-scope`, `mg-scope`, and `rg-scope` via `Set-AVMModule`.

- **Versioning and CHANGELOG**
  - Bumped the MINOR version in `version.json` from `0.1` to `0.2` for all three scopes (`sub-scope`, `mg-scope`, `rg-scope`).
  - Added a `## 0.2.0` section to each scope's `CHANGELOG.md` describing the new `notifications` parameter. This resolves the Module Compliance failure requiring the CHANGELOG to contain a section for the new module version.

```bicep
param notifications notificationType[]?

var notificationSettings = !empty(notifications ?? []) ? notifications! : notificationsFromThresholds

var notificationsArray = [
  for notification in notificationSettings: {
    '${notification.thresholdType}_${notification.operator}_${notification.threshold}_Percentage': {
      enabled: true
      operator: notification.operator
      threshold: notification.threshold
      thresholdType: notification.thresholdType
    }
  }
]
```

prs.author: segraef
prs.body:
Improves the agent guidance for contributing to AVM Bicep modules and makes it work across AI assistants, not just GitHub Copilot.

## Changes

- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`**: Added an explicit, mandatory ordered checklist for fixing an issue in an existing module - branch + contribution-model detection (maintainer direct-push vs fork), edit `main.bicep` only, bump `version.json`/`CHANGELOG.md`, regenerate `main.json` + `README.md` via `Set-AVMModule`, update e2e tests, local Pester gate before push, and e2e workflow + status badge on the PR. Also bumped the validated model to `Claude Opus 4.8` or `Fable`.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: Mirrors `.github/copilot-instructions.md` with an AGENTS.md-style header so non-Copilot agents (Claude Code, Cursor, and others) that read `AGENTS.md` get the same rules. Kept in sync with the instructions file.

## Why

Instructions are guidance, not enforcement, and agents were missing key steps (running `Set-AVMModule`, getting local tests green, attaching the e2e badge). The checklist makes those steps unmissable. `AGENTS.md` exists because non-Copilot assistants do not read `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so the operative rules are duplicated there rather than redirected.

## Description
This pull request expands the set of disabled TLS cipher suites in the API Management service modules to enhance security and align with best practices. It updates the default security configuration in both the Bicep and JSON templates, documentation, and related tests to explicitly disable several additional ECDHE and RSA cipher suites.
Fixes #6167 
The most important changes are:

**Security configuration updates:**

* Added the following cipher suites to the default set of disabled ciphers in `customProperties` and related configuration:
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384`
  * `TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`

**Documentation updates:**

* Updated `README.md` to document the new disabled cipher suites in all relevant code and configuration examples, ensuring users are aware of the expanded set of disabled ciphers. 

**Template and test updates:**

* Synchronized the changes in the generated ARM template (`main.json`) and end-to-end test configuration to reflect the updated set of disabled ciphers.

### Manual E2E validation — Anthropic partner-model deployment

I deployed the current PR head (`aef55b0`) using the existing `tests/e2e/ai-model-deployment-anthropic` configuration in a live subscription that has approved Anthropic quota.

The full deployment completed successfully:

- `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts` (`AIServices`, `S0`) — `Succeeded`
- `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments/claude-sonnet-4-6` (`GlobalStandard`, capacity `25`) — `Succeeded`

The validation also confirmed the following environmental constraints:

- **Region:** `claude-sonnet-4-6` version `1` with `GlobalStandard` must be deployed in a supported region. This test pins `swedencentral` because it is not available in the shared `australiaeast` test location.

prs.body:
## Description
This pull request introduces several new Bicep modules for Azure AI and search resources, as well as improvements to workflow automation and job execution controls. The most significant changes are the addition of reusable, parameterized modules to streamline the deployment of AI Foundry projects, AI model deployments, AI Search, and generic Cognitive Services resources. Additionally, workflow automation is enhanced with a new container migration workflow and improved job execution conditions for pull request labeling.

**New AI and Search Bicep Modules:**

* Added `ai-foundry-project.bicep`, a wrapper module for deploying an Azure AI Services account and an AI Foundry project, with outputs for resource IDs, endpoints, and identities.
* Added `ai-foundry-model-deployment.bicep` for deploying a single AI model to an existing AI Services account, supporting model format, version, RAI policy, and SKU configuration.
* Added `ai-foundry-connection.bicep` to create a parameterized connection on an AI Foundry project, supporting various categories (e.g., CognitiveSearch, AzureBlob) and authentication types.
* Added `ai-search.bicep`, which implements a two-step deployment pattern for Azure AI Search: a fast initial resource creation, followed by an AVM module update for full configuration and managed identity.
* Added `ai-services.bicep`, a generic AVM wrapper for deploying Cognitive Services accounts of various kinds (e.g., ContentSafety, Speech, OpenAI), with support for private networking and role assignments.

**Workflow Automation and Controls:**

* Introduced `.github/workflows/avm.ptn.sa.container-migration.yml`, a new workflow for AVM container migration with input parameters for validation and deployment control, and a two-job structure for initialization and execution.
* Updated `platform.set-avm-github-pr-labels.yml` to skip the label-setting job on forks, preventing failures due to missing GitHub App secrets and aligning with existing fork-handling patterns.

**Major feature and breaking changes:**

Managed identity-based `AcrPull` access is configured for the App Service and Container Instance, and public placeholder images are used for initial deployment. prs.author: krbar
prs.body:
## Description

## Description

Follow-up to [#6316](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/6316), which changed child module deployment names to use `uniqueString(subscription().id, resourceGroup().id, location)`. That value is **not unique enough** when deploying multiple instances of the same resource type into the same resource group simultaneously, causing deployment name collisions.

This PR applies the same fix already merged for `avm/res/operational-insights/workspace` in [#7249](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7249): the parent resource `name` is added to the `uniqueString()` inputs so each parent resource generates distinct child deployment names.

**Example change:**
```diff
- name: '${uniqueString(subscription().id, resourceGroup().id, location)}-subnet-${index}'
+ name: '${uniqueString(subscription().id, resourceGroup().id, location, name)}-subnet-${index}'
```

Additionally, this PR rolls in a few housekeeping updates across the touched modules:

- Bumped cross-module references to their latest published versions:
  - `avm/res/network/private-endpoint` → `0.12.1`
  - `avm/res/network/public-ip-address` → `0.13.0`
  - `avm/res/operations-management/solution`  → `0.3.1`
- Updated the telemetry deployment resource API version `Microsoft.Resources/deployments` from `2024-03-01` to `2025-04-01`.

No breaking changes.

> Note: The `avm/res/network/bastion-host` module is affected as well, but the fix will be added to #7188

## Description

Closes #7197

Covering #7199 in a branch for the `modelProviderData` addition part


The new test avm/res/cognitive-services/account/tests/e2e/ai-model-deployment-anthropic/main.test.bicep is failing upstream and needs troubleshooting. It has been validated in the module owner subscription. Therefore leveraging e2eignore to skip the test.

The following subscription requirements have been validated, however the test fails with `Status Message: Error occurred when subscribing to Marketplace: Marketplace Subscription purchase eligibility check failed, error message [This subscription is internal or sandbox. Only $0.00 products or test products can be purchased. Please select a different subscription to purchase paid, non-test offers]. (Code:UserError)`

- Region: claude-sonnet-4-6 version 1 with GlobalStandard must be deployed in a supported region. This test pins eastus2 because it is not available in the shared australiaeast test location.
- Subscription/quota: Anthropic partner-model deployment requires allocated Anthropic quota. Subscriptions showing 0/0 TPM cannot provision the model.
- Offer type: Anthropic/Claude quota is gated by subscription offer type. A Production EA subscription (offer MS-AZR-0017P) receives Anthropic quota; an Enterprise Dev/Test subscription (MS-AZR-0148P) shows the model in the catalog but has 0/0 TPM.

Hi @eriqua 👋

Ask: could you cancel the stuck run [31089932148](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) and re-dispatch on feat/cognitive-services-account-deployment-module-backup? I don't have dispatch/admin rights, so I can't do it myself. It got caught in yesterday's [GitHub Actions incident](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) and is now a zombie — stuck queued with 0 jobs, and GitHub won't let me cancel or re-run it. If it's easier to leave it, no worries — I'll wait for GitHub to auto-reap the queued run and re-run then.

I've tested the deployment locally and it works fine, so I'm confident a clean run will pass. Findings:

Module works: deployed the ai-model-deployment-anthropic test — account + claude-sonnet-4-6 (v1, Anthropic, GlobalStandard, cap 25) both Succeeded, and modelProviderData is accepted at API 2026-05-01.
Real prerequisite is Anthropic quota, not offer type: it deployed on a non-EA (Internal) sub that had quota (claude-sonnet-4-6 GlobalStandard, 80 TPM in eastus2/swedencentral); a 0/0 TPM sub fails. Suggest we word the README as "needs approved Anthropic quota (>0 TPM), verifiable via az cognitiveservices usage list" — EA is just one way to get it.
Why CI was red: preflight hit The deployment 'claude-sonnet-4-6' is in 'Failed' state, please delete it before creating a new one — a leftover failed deployment on the shared test account blocking re-runs. After deleting it (+ confirming quota) it cleared preflight; the later failures were just the Actions incident (Failed to resolve action download info), not the template.
Ignore in logs: Node 20→24 (runner annotation) and BCP037 modelProviderData (expected until the spec lands — Azure/azure-rest-api-specs#43610).

[UNRELEASED]
